classes.title: 10 CLASSICAL · The Sound Keeps Changing
classes.description: Medieval era–present: Written melodies become interwoven voices, harmonic drama and new instrumental colors; composed forms change how tension and return are heard. LED TO: Musique Concrète, Third Stream, Minimalism.
classes.listeningQuestion: How does the organizing principle of composed music change across many centuries?
classes.revelation: A recognizable work can organize attention through melody, interwoven voices, harmony, color or repeating process.
classes.contradiction: A tradition often heard as fixed survives through repeated changes to its rules.
classes.musicalArgument:
CLASSICAL

Classical music is a changing set of ways to organize sound. Across this survey, listen to melody becoming polyphony, polyphony becoming harmonic drama, and inherited forms being stretched until composers invent new relationships among rhythm, color and musical time.

VOICES BECOME STRUCTURE

Medieval chant begins with the authority of one melodic line. Additional voices create a different kind of attention: sustained notes support moving lines, and Renaissance counterpoint makes the whole emerge from independent parts.

HARMONY AND FORM

Baroque music builds momentum from bass patterns, ornament and contrasting ensembles. Haydn and Mozart make phrase, contrast and return especially clear. Beethoven turns small motifs into large arguments, opening a route toward Romantic music’s intimate songs, expansive orchestras and increasingly unsettled harmony.

MANY FUTURES

The twentieth-century selections refuse a single successor. Color and dissonance, vernacular rhythm, prepared piano and repeating pulses offer different answers to what composition can do. The contemporary ending lets a familiar ensemble become an unfamiliar sound world.

Listen for the revelation: the tradition survives by changing the rules of attention. Ask what holds each piece together, and hear that answer change across the course.

# 10 CLASSICAL · The Sound Keeps Changing

Prepared, unpublished. No service playlist or app link was created.

## Listening lesson

Question: How does the organizing principle of composed music change across many centuries?

Revelation: A recognizable work can organize attention through melody, interwoven voices, harmony, color or repeating process.

Contradiction: A tradition often heard as fixed survives through repeated changes to its rules.

Argument: CLASSICAL

Classical music is a changing set of ways to organize sound. Across this survey, listen to melody becoming polyphony, polyphony becoming harmonic drama, and inherited forms being stretched until composers invent new relationships among rhythm, color and musical time.

VOICES BECOME STRUCTURE

Medieval chant begins with the authority of one melodic line. Additional voices create a different kind of attention: sustained notes support moving lines, and Renaissance counterpoint makes the whole emerge from independent parts.

HARMONY AND FORM

Baroque music builds momentum from bass patterns, ornament and contrasting ensembles. Haydn and Mozart make phrase, contrast and return especially clear. Beethoven turns small motifs into large arguments, opening a route toward Romantic music’s intimate songs, expansive orchestras and increasingly unsettled harmony.

MANY FUTURES

The twentieth-century selections refuse a single successor. Color and dissonance, vernacular rhythm, prepared piano and repeating pulses offer different answers to what composition can do. The contemporary ending lets a familiar ensemble become an unfamiliar sound world.

Listen for the revelation: the tradition survives by changing the rules of attention. Ask what holds each piece together, and hear that answer change across the course.

Classical music is a changing set of ways to organize sound. Across this survey, listen to melody becoming polyphony, polyphony becoming harmonic drama, and inherited forms being stretched until composers invent new relationships among rhythm, color and musical time.

Medieval chant begins with the authority of one melodic line. Additional voices create a different kind of attention: sustained notes support moving lines, and Renaissance counterpoint makes the whole emerge from independent parts.

HARMONY AND FORM

Baroque music builds momentum from bass patterns, ornament and contrasting ensembles. Haydn and Mozart make phrase, contrast and return especially clear. Beethoven turns small motifs into large arguments, opening a route toward Romantic music’s intimate songs, expansive orchestras and increasingly unsettled harmony.

MANY FUTURES

The twentieth-century selections refuse a single successor. Color and dissonance, vernacular rhythm, prepared piano and repeating pulses offer different answers to what composition can do. The contemporary ending lets a familiar ensemble become an unfamiliar sound world.

Listen for the revelation: the tradition survives by changing the rules of attention. Ask what holds each piece together, and hear that answer change across the course.

CLASSICAL · The Sound Keeps Changing
- Shape: one long paper strip passes through three distinct folds, changing from a single edge to interlocking planes to an open asymmetrical structure. One continuous material, three different ways of organizing it. Artwork in the lower 55% of a square canvas with clear space below the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F3EAD8), flat and untinted; title ink (#6B2440) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #6B2440, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Prepared, unpublished. No service playlist or app link was created.

## Listening lesson

Question: What happens when the guitar keeps singing beneath the voice?

Revelation: Bright, overlapping guitar figures carry melody around the singer; ringing sustain makes even small bands feel expansive.

Contradiction: A bright surface can carry anxiety and ambiguity.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

JANGLE POP · The Guitar Becomes Another Voice
- Shape: two thin interwoven strips, one continuous and one notched, creating a third wavering edge between them. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1E1C1A), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: jangle_pop

classes.title: 80.40 UK GARAGE / 2-STEP · The Missing Kick Makes You Move
classes.description: 1995–present: Skipped kicks, swinging hats and clipped R&B vocals make the gaps dance. FROM: Garage House, Jungle, Contemporary R&B. LED TO: Grime, Dubstep, UKG / Jungle-Pop Revival.
classes.listeningQuestion: Why does removing a kick make the groove feel more alive?
classes.revelation: Two-step places emphasis in the gaps: the singer, bass and percussion negotiate a beat that never simply marches.
classes.contradiction: Omitting expected kicks can make a groove feel more propulsive rather than less complete.
classes.musicalArgument: Two-step places emphasis in the gaps: the singer, bass and percussion negotiate a beat that never simply marches.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

UK GARAGE / 2-STEP · The Missing Kick Makes You Move
- Shape: skipped paving The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#D6EAE4), flat and untinted; title ink (#29251F) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #29251F, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: uk_garage_2_step

# Palm-Wine

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
Bass, offbeat chords and melodic replies coexist inside one repeating picking pattern.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#palmwine).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.nathanielbraddock.com/projects/palmwine-session); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Compare early Ghanaian recorded guitar with Sierra Leonean maringa and later Ghanaian revival; keep acoustic interplay distinct from the electric highlife classes.
- Contradiction: An intimate social sound helped supply the grammar of much larger popular bands.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
8 selected candidate recordings, with 8 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Kumasi Trio — Amponash Part 1: Hear a short early acoustic guitar ensemble recording; establish the archive’s spelling rather than silently substituting a later Ya Amponsah cover. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/amponash-part-1/322911730?i=322912416&uo=4). The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.

The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. - Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.

The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

# Taarab

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The singer stretches and punctuates language while the ensemble frames each emotional turn.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#taarab).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://verbafricana.org/swahili/b-kijiti-author-and-context.htm); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Do not collapse taarab into one sound: compare early recorded Swahili address, orchestral clubs, Zanzibar female vocal authority and modern amplified exchange.
- Contradiction: An elite orchestral inheritance becomes a vehicle for ordinary lives and public argument.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

The arrangement enlarges the frame while the dialect, ornaments and conversational address keep the place audible.

# Raï

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The stretched vocal phrase survives changing accompaniment; the beat answers rather than smooths its grain.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#rai).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://ich.unesco.org/fr/RL/le-rai-chant-populaire-d-algerie-01894?RL=01894); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Move from the cheikha voice through Oranian brass and cassette pop into international production, retaining differences between original recordings and later remakes.
- Contradiction: Commercial polish can amplify a voice whose authority comes from rough directness.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
12 selected candidate recordings, with 12 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings

[Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/charrak-gatta/1334160958?i=1334161051). classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

RAÏ · The Voice Pushes Through the Circuit
- Shape: One weathered folding screen at lower left opens into three differently angled translucent panels; one continuous dark notch cuts through all panels. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: rai

classes.title: 31.01.1.1.1 ETHIO-JAZZ · The Mode Changes the Groove
classes.description: 1960s–present: Ethiopian melodic modes bend across jazz voicings, clipped horn figures, bass vamps and percussion; later groups stretch the same tonal tension. FROM: Afro-Cuban Jazz.
classes.listeningQuestion: What makes a groove recognizable before a singer names its language?
classes.revelation: A small intervallic shape reorganizes how familiar jazz and funk rhythms feel.
classes.contradiction: International instrumentation can make a highly local melodic logic more audible.
classes.musicalArgument: Make Mulatu's arranging central without equating all Ethiopian popular music with instrumental Ethio-jazz; compare adjacent singers only where the arrangement demonstrates the lesson.

classes.researchNotesText:
# Ethio-Jazz

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
A small intervallic shape reorganizes how familiar jazz and funk rhythms feel.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#ethiojazz).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://strut-records.co.uk/blogs/news/strut-records-2024-round-up); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Make Mulatu's arranging central without equating all Ethiopian popular music with instrumental Ethio-jazz; compare adjacent singers only where the arrangement demonstrates the lesson.
- Contradiction: International instrumentation can make a highly local melodic logic more audible.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
12 selected candidate recordings, with 12 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Mulatu Astatke — I Faram Gami I Faram: Hear the Afro-Cuban small-group groundwork before the modal language fully crystallizes. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/i-faram-gami-i-faram/1707703868?i=1707703869). Proposed sequence year 1966; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 2. Mulatu Astatke — Yèkèrmo Sèw: Hear the repeating minor-colored horn contour define a whole groove. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/y%C3%A8k%C3%A8rmo-s%C3%A8w/1804996894?i=1804996905&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1969; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 3. Mulatu Astatke — Yègellé Tezeta: Hear the bass vamp support a contrasting melodic shape. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/y%C3%A8gell%C3%A9-tezeta/1807098908?i=1807099299&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1969; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 4. Girma Bèyènè — Ené Nègn Bay Manèsh: Hear an arranger's song-based approach beside instrumental examples. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/ene-ne-gn-bay-mane-sh/78934984?i=78934839). Proposed sequence year 1970; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 5. Mulatu Astatke — Mulatu: Hear the recorded studio sound turn restraint into tension. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/mulatu-stereo-master/1225952989?i=1225953450&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1972; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 6. Gétatchèw Mèkurya — Yègènèt Muziqa: Compare the saxophone's more forceful, vocalized attack. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/ye-ge-ne-t-muziqa/78952714?i=78952490). Proposed sequence year 1972; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 7. Mulatu Astatke — Yèkatit: Hear the ensemble clarify rhythmic and modal counterweights. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/y%C3%A8katit-february/78928362?i=78928297&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1974; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 8. The Heliocentrics & Mulatu Astatke — Masenqo: Hear new studio textures answer the older composer's short motifs. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/masenqo/307556145?i=307556193). Proposed sequence year 2009; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 9. Mulatu Astatke — Green Africa: Hear late small-group interplay deepen the form. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/green-africa/357006462?i=357006470). Proposed sequence year 2010; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 10. Akalé Wubé — Ayalqem Tèdèngo: Hear another ensemble make the repertoire playable in its own sound. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/ayalqem-t%C3%A8d%C3%A8ngo-intro/367112595?i=367112634). Proposed sequence year 2010; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 11. Girma Beyene & Akalé Wubé — Mèslogn Nèbèr: Hear an earlier arranger return inside a later band's conversational groove. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/m%C3%A8slogn-n%C3%A8b%C3%A8r/1189067670?i=1189069094). Proposed sequence year 2017; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 12. Hailu Mergia — Lala Belu: Hear organ and compact trio improvisation extend the modal pocket. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/lala-belu/1313329534?i=1313329816). Proposed sequence year 2018; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.

### Inferences
- The sequence is chronological by proposed original/repertoire year, with later interpretations and archive dates distinguished. Each track has a separate listening job.

### Gaps
- Before publication, confirm exact recording versions and original chronology, then check availability again. Spotify matching and live playlist checks have not been performed.

## What remains before publication?

### Takeaway
No playlist has been created or modified. This research draft is not yet a service-verified publication.

### Cited Findings
- Raw US catalog responses are preserved in `catalog-raw/global-ethiojazz.json`; the [Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#ethiojazz) supplies genealogy.

### Inferences
- The title and cover concept can be debated independently of remaining catalog repairs.

### Gaps
- Spotify matching, image visual review or production, final original-master checks and publication approval remain.

## Final competition and catalog review

12 retained selections have US catalog title/performer matches. 6 have additional original-album/year metadata support; this does not replace a listening check. 12 are eligible for the future import text. No service publication has occurred.

### Candidate competition
- Mahmoud Ahmed — Erè Mèla Mèla: A major Ethiopian popular-song recording; keep the focus on the instrumental/arranging grammar rather than making the class an Ethiopian pop survey.
- Mulatu Astatke — Yèkèrmo Sèw (2025): A rerecording may close a developmental comparison but cannot stand in for the 1969 master.
- Mulatu Astatke — Alebela: The proposed 2025 title was not substantiated by the checked catalog; retain the earlier defining work rather than force a recent slot.
- Either/Orchestra — Aynotche Terabu: The requested Either/Orchestra title did not resolve to that ensemble. Its role is already demonstrated more securely by the contemporary Akalé Wubé and Heliocentrics recordings; do not accept Tezeta Band under its name.

Draw this

ETHIO-JAZZ · The Mode Changes the Groove

# Marabi

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The repeated chords are a platform for changing accents, lines and participants rather than a finished accompaniment.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#marabi).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://sahistory.org.za/archive/melody-freedom); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Early marabi is poorly represented by surviving commercial recordings. Use later documented carriers and transformations, openly labeling the class as an audible reconstruction rather than a complete 1920s discography.
- Contradiction: A foundational social practice survives more clearly through later recordings than through its earliest rooms.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
10 selected candidate recordings, with 9 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Chris McGregor & The Castle Lager Big Band — Kippie: Hear the repeating township theme enlarged into a big-band arrangement. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/kippie/1748840143?i=1748840313). Proposed sequence year 1963; Later recorded carrier or transformation of marabi; not a claim to document an unrecorded 1920s room.
- 2. The Jazz Dazzlers — Diepkloof Ekhaya: Hear a compact township-band cycle carry a marabi-derived rhythmic shape; the archival session date needs checking. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/diepkloof-ekhaya/1641723337?i=1641723802&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1964; Later recorded carrier or transformation of marabi; not a claim to document an unrecorded 1920s room.

- 4. Abdullah Ibrahim — Soweto: Hear a different cyclic foundation sustain the same expansive ensemble logic. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/soweto/310156684?i=310156791&uo=4). # Kwela

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
Breath, articulation and the repeated harmonic pocket make a modest instrument rhythmically expansive.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#kwela).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://esat.sun.ac.za/index.php/Kwela); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Give the 1950s whistle players the defining weight, then compare saxophone and revival extensions; do not turn the lesson into a general township-jazz survey.
- Contradiction: A portable street sound becomes an international recording style without requiring a large ensemble.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
10 selected candidate recordings, with 10 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

KWELA · A Small Whistle Leads the Street
- Shape: One small folded-paper bird at lower left lifts a broad strip of pavement into a playful upward fold; three translucent paving slabs follow its changing angle. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: kwela

classes.title: 72.39.2 MBAQANGA · The Voices Bounce Against the Guitar
classes.description: 1960s–present: Clipped electric guitar and bass cycles support high female harmonies answered by a deep male lead; the groove keeps each part distinct. FROM: Marabi, Kwela. LED TO: Worldbeat, Township Bubblegum.
classes.listeningQuestion: How do a bass voice and bright female harmony become a single rhythmic engine?

# Mbaqanga

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The repeated guitar cycle does not flatten the singing; the contrast of registers makes the beat spring.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#mbaqanga).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.gov.za/about-government/mahlathini-simon-nkabinde-1938-1999); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Follow the studio band and vocal teams before their international revival; distinguish vocal mbaqanga from neighboring kwela and later electronic bubblegum.
- Contradiction: A studio-made dance sound carries local language and older vocal practices into a modern electric ensemble.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
12 selected candidate recordings, with 12 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Dark City Sisters — Letlapa Labutsoa: Hear female harmony ride a short, buoyant electric pattern. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/letlapa-labutsoa/1219988561?i=1219988811&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1964; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 2. Makgona Tsohle Band — Vula Bops: Isolate the instrumental ensemble that underpins the vocal dance sound. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/vula-bops/208256440?i=208257184). Proposed sequence year 1964; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 3. Mahlathini & The Mahotella Queens — Thoko: Hear the lead growl interrupt and energize the female response. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/thoko/1641635192?i=1641635395). Proposed sequence year 1964; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 4. Mahlathini & The Mahotella Queens — Umculo Kawupheli: Hear the recurring cycle support variation in vocal attack. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/umculo-kawupheli/1620399176?i=1620399178). Proposed sequence year 1973; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 5. Dark City Sisters — Siyagiya: Compare a female-led arrangement without the same lead-vocal contrast. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/siyagiya/1631700733?i=1631701111). Proposed sequence year 1973; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 6. Mahlathini and The Mahotella Queens — Kazet: Hear the revitalized ensemble sharpen its bass and vocal exchanges. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/kazet/1569884284?i=1569884285). Proposed sequence year 1987; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 7. Mahlathini and The Mahotella Queens — Lilizela Mlilizeli: Hear an extended vocal and instrumental conversation from the classic ensemble’s revival. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/lilizela-mlilizeli/1627831513?i=1627831526&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1987; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 8. Mahlathini and The Mahotella Queens — Melodi Yalla: Hear the touring-era band make its interlocking parts especially clear. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/melodi-ya-lla/1569884284?i=1569884559&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1988; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 9. Mahlathini and The Mahotella Queens — Re Ya Dumedisa: Hear a different choral entrance and lead-response pattern from the revived band. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/re-ya-dumedisa/1004018173?i=1004018658). Proposed sequence year 1988; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 10. Mahlathini and The Mahotella Queens — Jive Motella: Hear a mature ensemble vary the refrain without abandoning the cycle. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/jive-motella/895278099?i=895278244). Proposed sequence year 1990; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 11. Mahotella Queens — Mbube: Hear the vocal ensemble recast an older song rather than use a generic new chorus. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/mbube/1641635192?i=1641635197). - 12. Mahotella Queens — Town Hall: Hear the established phrasing carry into a late collective performance. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/town-hall/1641638961?i=1641639528). Proposed sequence year 2004; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.

### Inferences
- The sequence is chronological by proposed original/repertoire year, with later interpretations and archive dates distinguished. Each track has a separate listening job.

### Gaps

## What remains before publication?

### Takeaway
No playlist has been created or modified. This research draft is not yet a service-verified publication.

### Cited Findings
- Raw US catalog responses are preserved in `catalog-raw/global-mbaqanga.json`; the [Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#mbaqanga) supplies genealogy.

### Inferences
- The title and cover concept can be debated independently of remaining catalog repairs.

### Gaps
- Spotify matching, image visual review or production, final original-master checks and publication approval remain.

## Final competition and catalog review

12 retained selections have US catalog title/performer matches. 4 have additional original-album/year metadata support; this does not replace a listening check. 12 are eligible for the future import text. No service publication has occurred.

### Candidate competition
- Paul Simon — Gumboots: The source ensemble matters, but the international pop adaptation should not displace the South African class's own defining music.
- Brenda Fassie — Weekend Special: A strong bubblegum successor, reserved for that focused class.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

MBAQANGA · The Voices Bounce Against the Guitar
- Shape: One low wooden seesaw carries a broad heavy block at one end and three narrow upright blocks at the other, caught in a balanced rebound. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: mbaqanga

classes.researchNotesText:
# Township Bubblegum

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The hook is built from exchanged voices as much as from the synthesizer line.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#sa_bubblegum).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://musicinafrica.net/node/12958); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Compare the defining singers and producers across early disco-pop, politically coded songs and the rhythmic space that precedes kwaito.
- Contradiction: Music dismissed as disposable pop can carry sharp social pressure.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
12 selected candidate recordings, with 12 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

TOWNSHIP BUBBLEGUM · The Synth Keeps the Township Singing
- Shape: One brightly painted corrugated storefront shutter at lower left rolls up in three overlapping translucent folds, revealing a dark open rectangle rather than a scene. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: township_bubblegum

classes.researchNotesText:
# Mbalax

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The pulse is steady, but the drum accents and sung phrase make the surface continuously change direction.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#mbalax).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://musicinafrica.net/node/14993); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Begin with Afro-Cuban band context, then hear the Wolof-language and sabar-centered transformation before comparing distinct singers and pop-facing mutations.
- Contradiction: A style can absorb international pop while remaining rhythmically difficult to reduce to its backbeat.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
12 selected candidate recordings, with 12 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Étoile de Dakar — Thiely: Hear the young lead voice stretch beyond an inherited band pattern. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/thiely/977536796?i=977536802). Proposed sequence year 1978; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.

- Baaba Maal — Yela: A neighboring Senegalese tradition, not a substitute for the Wolof mbalax story.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

MBALAX · The Drum Makes the Melody Turn
- Shape: One interlocking wooden puzzle at lower left turns around a single off-center peg; three broad translucent pieces swing outward without leaving the shared center. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: mbalax

# Soukous

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The guitar's short figures become an extended conversation; propulsion grows through interlock rather than a heavier backbeat.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#soukous).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://musicinafrica.net/node/141783); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Move from rumba's composed song and sebene contrast into guitar-centered transnational dance records, then end before ndombolo becomes the whole story.
- Contradiction: A song can become more repetitive and more eventful at the same time.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
12 selected candidate recordings, with 12 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

Draw this

SOUKOUS · The Guitar Opens the Dance Section
- Shape: One pair of interlocking metal zipper halves at lower left opens into a wide branching fabric pleat; the seam remains visible as the pleat spreads beyond the right edge. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: soukous

# Ndombolo

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The caller shapes entrances, motion and expectation rather than merely commenting over the music.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#ndombolo).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://musicinafrica.net/node/141783); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Distinguish ndombolo's dance-centered late-1990s crystallization from earlier soukous; compare rival band languages and later solo stars without reducing the scene to one artist.
- Contradiction: A fast dance can depend on tightly controlled space and repeated cues.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
12 selected candidate recordings, with 12 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

NDOMBOLO · The Call Turns the Band into Motion
- Shape: One folding hand fan at lower left snaps open across three positions; its ribs are broad countable shapes, with a single dark tab directing the movement. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: ndombolo

# Classic Female Blues

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The voice can lead, delay and provoke the ensemble rather than simply sit on its accompaniment.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#classic_blues).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://folkways.si.edu/lesson/blues-royalty/women-who-ruled-the-blues); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Center the women whose theater, vaudeville and recording careers established the classic blues market; compare vocal agency, accompaniment and social persona rather than making a compilation of interchangeable laments.
- Contradiction: Commercial stages and records become platforms for unusually direct self-definition.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

CLASSIC FEMALE BLUES · The Singer Takes the Public Stage
- Shape: One unoccupied theater lectern at lower left casts an enormous slanted shadow shaped as an open doorway; two translucent curtain panels part behind it. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F3A6E), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

# Piedmont Blues

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
An independent bass line allows melody and voice to anticipate, delay and answer the beat.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#piedmont).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://folkways.si.edu/magazine-winter-2018-blues-legacy-of-phil-wiggins); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Follow different fingerpicking architectures, not a geographic list alone; compare ragtime fluency, gospel adaptation, guitar-harmonica dialogue and later continuity.
- Contradiction: A relaxed surface can depend on exceptionally exact coordination.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

PIEDMONT BLUES · The Thumb Keeps a Second Conversation
- Shape: One small wooden box at lower left opens in two directions at once; a steady row of broad dark tabs anchors the base while three colored lids pivot independently. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F3A6E), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: piedmont_blues

classes.title: 40.01.5 BOOGIE-WOOGIE · The Left Hand Builds the Engine
classes.description: 1920s–present: Repeated bass figures drive the piano while the right hand riffs, answers and breaks away; the same motor can support solo display, singing or a full band. FROM: Country Blues, Ragtime. LED TO: Jump Blues, Rhythm and Blues, New Orleans R&B.
classes.listeningQuestion: How does the pianist make repetition feel like acceleration?
classes.revelation: The bass supplies continuity while accents, register and right-hand variation make the surface intensify.
classes.contradiction: Mechanical regularity is the platform for highly individual touch.
classes.musicalArgument: Separate the repeating piano technique from any generic fast blues; compare bass patterns, solo and ensemble roles, and its migration toward jump blues and rock and roll.

# Boogie-Woogie

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The bass supplies continuity while accents, register and right-hand variation make the surface intensify.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#boogie).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.loc.gov/static/programs/national-recording-preservation-board/documents/HonkyTonkTrainBlues.pdf); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Separate the repeating piano technique from any generic fast blues; compare bass patterns, solo and ensemble roles, and its migration toward jump blues and rock and roll.
- Contradiction: Mechanical regularity is the platform for highly individual touch.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
16 selected candidate recordings, with 16 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Jimmy Blythe — Chicago Stomp: Hear an early recorded repeating bass organize a compact piano dance. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/chicago-stomp/203061373?i=203061396). Proposed sequence year 1924; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 2. Meade Lux Lewis — Honky Tonk Train Blues: Hear bass motion and register turn the piano into a changing rhythmic environment. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/honky-tonk-train-blues/91806298?i=91806096). Proposed sequence year 1927; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 3. Pinetop Smith — Pine Top's Boogie Woogie: Hear spoken dance instruction and the piano motor become a single performance. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/pinetops-boogie-woogie-remastered/569992556?i=569992557). Proposed sequence year 1928; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 4. Cow Cow Davenport — Cow Cow Blues: Compare a different left-hand pattern and attack. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/cow-cow-blues-take-a/81721817?i=81721103). Proposed sequence year 1928; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 5. Albert Ammons — Boogie Woogie Stomp: Hear a more forceful attack propel the right-hand riff. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/boogie-woogie-stomp/1235943311?i=1235943319). Proposed sequence year 1936; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 6. Pete Johnson & Big Joe Turner — Roll 'Em Pete: Hear the voice ride and answer the pianist's repeating engine. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/roll-em-pete/300931322?i=300931507). Proposed sequence year 1938; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 7. Albert Ammons & Meade Lux Lewis — Boogie Woogie Prayer: Hear two pianists coordinate momentum without simply doubling each other. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/boogie-woogie-prayer/282464232?i=282464253). Proposed sequence year 1938; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 8. Jimmy Yancey — Yancey Stomp: Hear restraint and an idiosyncratic bass shape make a distinct pocket. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/yancey-stomp/351166269?i=351166277). Proposed sequence year 1939; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 9. Freddie Slack — Down the Road a Piece: Hear the piano technique enter an ensemble and a concise popular song. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/down-the-road-a-piece/1443115140?i=1443116149). Proposed sequence year 1940; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 10. Pete Johnson — Death Ray Boogie: Hear rapid right-hand figures intensify a firmly maintained bass. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/death-ray-boogie/1259419809?i=1259420304). Proposed sequence year 1941; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 11. Hadda Brooks — Swingin' the Boogie: Hear a pianist with a different touch maintain rhythmic authority. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/swingin-the-boogie/715908147?i=715908439). Proposed sequence year 1945; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 12. Camille Howard — X-Temporaneous Boogie: Hear the piano drive the jump-band era from within. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/x-temporaneous-boogie/1443310365?i=1443310376). Proposed sequence year 1948; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 13. Professor Longhair — Tipitina: Hear the boogie motor altered by a New Orleans rhythmic accent. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/tipitina/160594017?i=160594211). Proposed sequence year 1953; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 14. Jerry Lee Lewis — Whole Lotta Shakin' Goin' On: Hear the inherited piano engine and vocal breaks become rock and roll. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/whole-lotta-shakin-goin-on/1454735027?i=1454735252). Proposed sequence year 1957; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 15. Katie Webster — Two-Fisted Mama: Hear a later master make left-hand force and vocal command mutually reinforcing. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/two-fisted-mama/1881162414?i=1881162415). Proposed sequence year 1989; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 16. Marcia Ball — Red Hot: Hear a continuing piano tradition connect precision to band interaction. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/red-hot/1443721668?i=1443722420). Proposed sequence year 2001; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.

### Inferences
- The sequence is chronological by proposed original/repertoire year, with later interpretations and archive dates distinguished. Each track has a separate listening job.

### Gaps
- Before publication, confirm exact recording versions and original chronology, then check availability again. Spotify matching and live playlist checks have not been performed.

## What remains before publication?

### Takeaway
No playlist has been created or modified. This research draft is not yet a service-verified publication.

### Cited Findings
- Raw US catalog responses are preserved in `catalog-raw/global-boogie.json`; the [Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#boogie) supplies genealogy.

### Inferences
- The title and cover concept can be debated independently of remaining catalog repairs.

### Gaps
- Spotify matching, image visual review or production, final original-master checks and publication approval remain.

## Final competition and catalog review

16 retained selections have US catalog title/performer matches. 1 have additional original-album/year metadata support; this does not replace a listening check. 16 are eligible for the future import text. No service publication has occurred.

### Candidate competition
- Meade Lux Lewis — Honky Tonk Train Blues later remake: Different takes must not be assigned the 1927 date without verifying the master.
- Jools Holland — A generic fast blues: Speed alone does not demonstrate an independent repeating boogie bass.

Source correction: use the [Smithsonian Jazz Piano booklet](https://folkways-media.si.edu/docs/folkways/artwork/SFW40820.pdf), not an unconfirmed guessed Library of Congress filename.
