Draw this

BOOGIE-WOOGIE · The Left Hand Builds the Engine
- Shape: One small hand-cranked conveyor at lower left carries four broad blocks upward; its repeating tread is steady while each block tips at a different angle. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F3A6E), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: boogie_woogie

classes.researchNotesText:
# West Coast Blues

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
A carefully placed guitar phrase or delayed syllable can carry more weight than continuous volume.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#westcoast_blues).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.arts.gov/honors/heritage/charles-brown); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Show the California/Texas migration, contrasting pianists and guitarists, and later keepers; do not confuse a geographic address with one uniform arrangement.
- Contradiction: Urban polish need not soften the blues' emotional pressure.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
16 selected candidate recordings, with 15 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Johnny Moore's Three Blazers — Drifting Blues: Hear Charles Brown's intimate piano-vocal balance in a small ensemble. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/drifting-blues-digitally-remastered/435326381?i=435326385). Proposed sequence year 1945; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.

WEST COAST BLUES · The Guitar Leaves Room for the Voice
- Shape: One narrow balcony at lower left projects over a broad empty opening; three translucent awnings at different heights leave carefully measured gaps. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F3A6E), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.title: 72.35 CAJUN · The Bow and Bellows Share the Dance
classes.description: 1920s–present: Accordion and fiddle trade a flexible melody above a firm two-step or waltz; French singing and tightly coordinated ensemble accents keep the dancers turning. LED TO: Creole la-la, Swamp Pop.
classes.listeningQuestion: How do melody instruments agree on the dance while keeping different kinds of motion?
classes.revelation: The fiddle can stretch and ornament while the accordion gives the phrase a strong rhythmic edge.
classes.contradiction: A regional dance tradition renews itself by changing instrumentation without surrendering its phrasing.
classes.musicalArgument: Follow early commercial sides, string-band expansion, the accordion revival and later bands; preserve original recordings where available and identify later revival interpretations honestly.

# Cajun

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The fiddle can stretch and ornament while the accordion gives the phrase a strong rhythmic edge.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#cajun).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://musicrising.tulane.edu/discover/people/breaux-cleoma-falcon/); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Follow early commercial sides, string-band expansion, the accordion revival and later bands; preserve original recordings where available and identify later revival interpretations honestly.
- Contradiction: A regional dance tradition renews itself by changing instrumentation without surrendering its phrasing.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
16 selected candidate recordings, with 16 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Joe Falcon & Cléoma Breaux — Allons à Lafayette: Hear voice, guitar and accordion establish a compact two-step. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/allons-%C3%A0-lafayette/1509382692?i=1509383355). Proposed sequence year 1928; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 2. Dennis McGee & Sady Courville — Mon Chère Bébé Créole: Hear twin fiddles organize the melody without relying on accordion. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/mon-ch%C3%A8re-b%C3%A9b%C3%A9-cr%C3%A9ole/1574015413?i=1574015414). Proposed sequence year 1929; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 3. Amédée Breaux — Ma Blonde Est Partie: Hear the early waltz shape that later versions will reshape. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/ma-blonde-est-partie/201412093?i=201412464). Proposed sequence year 1929; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 4. Hackberry Ramblers — Jolie Blonde: Hear string-band and swing instrumentation alter the older melody. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/jolie-blonde-version-1/1706581989?i=1706582970). Proposed sequence year 1936; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.

[Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/hand-me-down-my-walking-cane/1096703407?i=1096704462&uo=4). - 6. Harry Choates — Jole Blon: Hear a fiddle-led performance sharpen its dance-band attack. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/jole-blon/327435367?i=327435371). - 7. Iry LeJeune — Love Bridge Waltz: Hear an insistent accordion and highly ornamented vocal restore an older balance. Proposed sequence year 2017; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.

- The sequence is chronological by proposed original/repertoire year, with later interpretations and archive dates distinguished. Each track has a separate listening job.

### Gaps

### Takeaway
No playlist has been created or modified. This research draft is not yet a service-verified publication.

### Cited Findings
- Raw US catalog responses are preserved in `catalog-raw/global-cajun.json`; the [Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#cajun) supplies genealogy.

### Inferences
- The title and cover concept can be debated independently of remaining catalog repairs.

### Gaps
- Spotify matching, image visual review or production, final original-master checks and publication approval remain.

## Final competition and catalog review

16 retained selections have US catalog title/performer matches. 2 have additional original-album/year metadata support; this does not replace a listening check. 16 are eligible for the future import text. No service publication has occurred.

### Candidate competition
- Clifton Chenier — I'm Coming Home: Zydeco deserves its own rhythmic and social story; do not substitute it for Cajun music.
- Harry Choates — Jole Blon later cover: A later singer's version does not establish Choates's 1946 breakthrough.

- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: cajun

# Creole la-la

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The attack of bow and bellows makes flexible time audible inside a repetitive tune.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#creole).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.arts.gov/honors/heritage/alphonse-bois-sec-ardoin); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Do not treat Creole la-la as merely early zydeco or simply Cajun music by another name. Give Ardoin and later Creole carriers enough space; document archival recording dates carefully.
- Contradiction: A foundational regional sound is often heard through later carriers and neighboring genre names.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
11 selected candidate recordings, with 11 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Amédé Ardoin & Dennis McGee — Two Step de Eunice: Hear accordion and fiddle interlock around an insistent vocal phrase. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/two-step-de-eunice/201412093?i=201413393). Proposed sequence year 1929; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.

### Takeaway
No playlist has been created or modified. This research draft is not yet a service-verified publication.

### Cited Findings
- Raw US catalog responses are preserved in `catalog-raw/global-creole.json`; the [Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#creole) supplies genealogy.

- The title and cover concept can be debated independently of remaining catalog repairs.

- Spotify matching, image visual review or production, final original-master checks and publication approval remain.

11 retained selections have US catalog title/performer matches. 4 have additional original-album/year metadata support; this does not replace a listening check. 11 are eligible for the future import text. No service publication has occurred.

### Candidate competition
- Clifton Chenier — Zydeco Sont Pas Salés: A useful descendant, but already belongs to a focused Zydeco class.
- Cajun revival bands — A second generic waltz: Shared repertoire alone does not demonstrate the Creole vocal and ensemble argument.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

CREOLE LA-LA · The Squeeze Answers the Bow
- Shape: One weathered wooden hinge at lower left joins two differently angled panels; their broad translucent shadows overlap into a third shape that neither panel makes alone. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

# Calypso

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
A singer can delay a word, sharpen a rhyme and change the social force of an otherwise familiar pulse.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#calypso).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.carnegiehall.org/Education/Programs/Musical-Explorers/Digital/Program-Eight/Etienne); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Center Trinidadian calypsonians rather than equating calypso with the US craze; follow topical verse, competition, gendered answer songs and the move toward soca.
- Contradiction: A playful surface can carry a pointed public dispute.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

CALYPSO · The Verse Reports Back to the Street
- Shape: One small street bulletin board at lower left tips forward as three oversized folded notices peel off and overlap, each with large blank color fields and no writing. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F4D36), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: calypso

classes.title: 72.36 SAMBA · The Song Dances Around the Pulse
classes.description: 1910s–present: Percussion, syncopated strings and conversational melody keep a steady dance pulse in motion; a sung phrase can lean ahead, sit back or answer the chorus. LED TO: Bossa Nova.
classes.listeningQuestion: How can a steady beat keep feeling off balance?
classes.revelation: The tune, bass and percussion occupy different sides of the pulse, making swing from their conversation.
classes.contradiction: A national emblem remains a set of changing local practices rather than one fixed rhythm.
classes.musicalArgument: Trace recorded urban samba, composer-led song, intimate samba and renewed percussion-centered groups; show variation without treating bossa nova or all Brazilian pop as interchangeable.

# Samba

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The tune, bass and percussion occupy different sides of the pulse, making swing from their conversation.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#samba).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/samba-de-roda-of-the-reconcavo-of-bahia-00101); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Trace recorded urban samba, composer-led song, intimate samba and renewed percussion-centered groups; show variation without treating bossa nova or all Brazilian pop as interchangeable.
- Contradiction: A national emblem remains a set of changing local practices rather than one fixed rhythm.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
18 selected candidate recordings, with 18 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

[Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/pelo-telefone/1706590823?i=1706590833&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1917; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

SAMBA · The Song Dances Around the Pulse
- Shape: One round café tray at lower left tilts while three differently shaped cups slide along its rim and maintain a balanced, circular path; no hands or writing. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.researchNotesText:
# Protestant Hymnody

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
Repetition, range and cadence make the song learnable; different communities then give those same features distinctive weight.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#hymns).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.loc.gov/collections/songs-of-america/articles-and-essays/musical-styles/ritual-and-worship/protestant-hymns/); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Sequence selected repertoire by composition/publication chronology, with later recording dates separately disclosed. This is a hymnody class, not a claim that modern performances were recorded in the eighteenth century.
- Contradiction: A fixed printed tune can support remarkably different social sounds.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
10 selected candidate recordings, with 10 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. The Choir of King's College Cambridge — When I Survey the Wondrous Cross: Hear regular stanzas and balanced cadence in a formal choral setting. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/when-i-survey-the-wondrous-cross-1994-remastered-version/696679329?i=696680271). Proposed sequence year 1707; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.
- 2. Indian Bottom Association — I'm Not Ashamed to Own My Lord: Hear shared text become communal ornamented sound rather than synchronized choral delivery. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/im-not-ashamed-to-own-my-lord/118382349?i=118385365&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1709; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.
- 3. The Choir of King's College Cambridge — O God Our Help in Ages Past: Hear common meter make a large public declaration singable. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/o-god-our-help-in-ages-past/1453010267?i=1453010420). Proposed sequence year 1719; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.
- 4. Indian Bottom Association — Guide Me O Thou Great Jehovah: Hear a leader’s line answered and stretched by a congregation; compare this participatory timing with the choral examples. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/guide-me-o-thou-great-jehovah/118382349?i=118384741&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1745; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.
- 5. The Choir of King's College Cambridge — Love Divine All Loves Excelling: Hear longer melodic phrases remain learnable through repetition and cadence. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/love-divine-all-loves-excelling/1453010267?i=1453010413). Proposed sequence year 1747; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.
- 6. Anonymous 4 — Wondrous Love: Hear a professional quartet illuminate an American hymn’s spare intervallic structure; identify this as a modern interpretation. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/wondrous-love/586106122?i=586106230&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1811; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.
- 7. Mahalia Jackson — Abide With Me: Hear a gospel soloist stretch the same durable hymn language into personal vocal testimony. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/abide-with-me/190183806?i=190184442&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1847; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.
- 8. The Alabama Sacred Harp Singers — Antioch: Hear strong independent parts and full-voiced communal attack differ from the English cathedral blend. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/antioch/459051919?i=459052332&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1850; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.
- 9. Doc & Merle Watson — What a Friend We Have In Jesus: Hear a familiar congregational text move into an intimate acoustic family-duo setting. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/what-a-friend-we-have-in-jesus/712209122?i=712209457&uo=4). Proposed sequence year 1855; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.
- 10. The Choir of King's College Cambridge — The Day Thou Gavest Lord Is Ended: Hear the evening hymn close through sustained collective breathing and a stable stanza. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/the-day-thou-gavest-lord-is-ended/1453010267?i=1453011074). Proposed sequence year 1870; Repertoire/text chronology, not historical recording chronology. The modern choral performance is explicitly later.

### Inferences
- The sequence is chronological by proposed original/repertoire year, with later interpretations and archive dates distinguished. Each track has a separate listening job.

### Gaps
- Hymn chronology follows repertoire/text publication, with cathedral, lined-out Baptist, shape-note, gospel-solo and acoustic-duo interpretations identified as later recordings; confirm tune dates separately.
- Before publication, confirm exact recording versions and original chronology, then check availability again. Spotify matching and live playlist checks have not been performed.

## What remains before publication?

### Takeaway
No playlist has been created or modified. This research draft is not yet a service-verified publication.

### Cited Findings
- Raw US catalog responses are preserved in `catalog-raw/global-hymns.json`; the [Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#hymns) supplies genealogy.

### Inferences
- The title and cover concept can be debated independently of remaining catalog repairs.

### Gaps
- Spotify matching, image visual review or production, final original-master checks and publication approval remain.

## Final competition and catalog review

10 retained selections have US catalog title/performer matches. 0 have additional original-album/year metadata support; this does not replace a listening check. 10 are eligible for the future import text. No service publication has occurred.

### Candidate competition
- Instrumental hymn medleys — Various: Without shared words and breathing, they hide the central congregational argument.
- One choir only — A complete hymn anthology: Replaced by contrasting cathedral, lined-out Baptist, shape-note, gospel-solo and acoustic-duo practices.

Text dates sequence the repertoire, not the age of the melody sounding. The label booklet dates BLAENWERN to 1905 despite Love Divine’s 1747 text. Exact selected tunes remain separately unconfirmed where the selected catalog edition lacks a booklet. Lined-out Baptist, shape-note, gospel-solo and acoustic-duo recordings are later living practices, not eighteenth-century recordings.

classes.title: 60.06.1 SOUTHERN GOSPEL · Four Parts Carry the Refrain
classes.description: 1910s–present: Close lead, tenor, baritone and bass parts turn a clear melody into rhythmic exchange; piano runs and family harmonies enlarge the song's testimony. FROM: Protestant Hymnody. LED TO: Jesus Music.
classes.listeningQuestion: How do four assigned vocal parts create movement inside a simple refrain?
classes.revelation: The bass and tenor do rhythmic as well as harmonic work; their entrances make the song feel physically lifted.
classes.contradiction: A carefully arranged commercial performance can still address listeners as a shared testimony.
classes.musicalArgument: Compare quartet conventions, family groups and later mixed ensembles; do not flatten Southern Gospel into either all white religious music or the separate Black gospel-quartet tradition.

# Southern Gospel

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

SOUTHERN GOSPEL · Four Parts Carry the Refrain
- Shape: One four-section wooden folding ladder at lower left opens into a single rising zigzag, with each broad rung a contrasting color and no people. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#687236), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.musicalArgument: Begin with clear gospel/R&B crossings, give the 1990s choir-and-hip-hop synthesis defining weight, then follow varied later approaches instead of treating one producer as the entire genre.

# Urban Contemporary Gospel

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
Massed voices punctuate rhythm and supply hooks, while the lead keeps the flexible force of gospel testimony.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#urbangospel).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://kirkfranklin.com/); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Begin with clear gospel/R&B crossings, give the 1990s choir-and-hip-hop synthesis defining weight, then follow varied later approaches instead of treating one producer as the entire genre.
- Contradiction: Club-ready production and collective sacred address can occupy the same arrangement.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
17 selected candidate recordings, with 17 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. The Winans — The Question Is: Hear close gospel harmony take on a carefully arranged modern band sound. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/the-question-is/252142879?i=252142940). Proposed sequence year 1981; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 2. Commissioned — Running Back to You: Hear a vocal group combine gospel inflection and an R&B ballad frame. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/running-back-to-you/337180483?i=337180725). Proposed sequence year 1986; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.

## What remains before publication?

### Takeaway
No playlist has been created or modified. This research draft is not yet a service-verified publication.

### Cited Findings
- Raw US catalog responses are preserved in `catalog-raw/global-urbangospel.json`; the [Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#urbangospel) supplies genealogy.

### Inferences
- The title and cover concept can be debated independently of remaining catalog repairs.

- Spotify matching, image visual review or production, final original-master checks and publication approval remain.

## Final competition and catalog review

17 retained selections have US catalog title/performer matches. 7 have additional original-album/year metadata support; this does not replace a listening check. 17 are eligible for the future import text. No service publication has occurred.

### Candidate competition
- Kirk Franklin — Every hit single: Several developmental roles justify repeats, but the class must retain distinct singers, choirs and arranging approaches.
- Tye Tribbett — A live medley of several songs: A medley complicates import matching and hides individual arrangement decisions.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

URBAN CONTEMPORARY GOSPEL · The Choir Rides the New Groove
- Shape: One long communal dining table at lower left breaks into three staggered but connected sections; broad translucent tablecloth corners interlock as the sections shift. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#687236), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: urban_contemporary_gospel

classes.researchNotesText:
# Christian Rock

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The riff can argue and build tension, rather than merely accompany a religious message.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#christianrock).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.gmahalloffame.org/); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Trace distinct band languages from hard rock through alternative rock and heavier modern production; describe the shared market without pretending that every Christian artist makes the same sound.
- Contradiction: A market defined by belief contains several different musical languages.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

CHRISTIAN ROCK · The Testimony Takes the Riff
- Shape: One heavy hinged gate at lower left swings open against a broad slanted wooden brace; three translucent positions make its resistance and release visible. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#687236), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.title: 60.05.2 CONTEMPORARY CHRISTIAN (CCM) · The Personal Song Finds a Shared Radio
classes.description: 1970s–present: Clear lead melodies, polished keyboards and intimate testimony meet pop songcraft; later productions change the groove while keeping direct personal address. FROM: Jesus Music, Soft Rock. LED TO: Christian Hip Hop, Praise & Worship.
classes.listeningQuestion: How does a song become personal testimony and radio-scale pop at once?
classes.revelation: Production changes, but the voice keeps presenting the song as an immediate personal encounter.
classes.contradiction: A commercially organized genre can contain both confession and broad crossover ambition.
classes.musicalArgument: Differentiate the CCM industry/format from a single musical style; choose audible milestones in voice, arrangement and crossover without treating sales alone as the musical argument.

# Contemporary Christian (CCM)

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
Production changes, but the voice keeps presenting the song as an immediate personal encounter.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#ccm).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.georgiaencyclopedia.org/articles/arts-culture/amy-grant-b-1960/); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Differentiate the CCM industry/format from a single musical style; choose audible milestones in voice, arrangement and crossover without treating sales alone as the musical argument.
- Contradiction: A commercially organized genre can contain both confession and broad crossover ambition.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

CONTEMPORARY CHRISTIAN (CCM) · The Personal Song Finds a Shared Radio
- Shape: One small open diary at lower left unfolds into an oversized blank window; three broad colored panes overlap while the book's original spine stays visible. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#687236), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: contemporary_christian_ccm

classes.title: 60.05.2.1 PRAISE & WORSHIP · The Chorus Gives the Room a Voice
classes.description: 1970s–present: Short melodic phrases, repeatable words and gentle harmonic cycles turn a lead singer's address into a whole room's shared song. FROM: Contemporary Christian (CCM), Protestant Hymnody. LED TO: Modern Worship.
classes.listeningQuestion: What makes a newly written song immediately usable by a congregation?
classes.revelation: The leader leaves room for other voices; repetition is a practical invitation rather than merely a hook.
classes.contradiction: A commercial recording can be organized around participation rather than virtuoso display.
classes.musicalArgument: Choose original or defining leader recordings where possible. Live room sound is often evidence of the central musical function and should not automatically be replaced by a studio remake.

# Praise & Worship

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
The leader leaves room for other voices; repetition is a practical invitation rather than merely a hook.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#worship).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://www.worshipfuel.com/equip/an-interview-with-modern-day-worship-music-pioneer-don-moen/); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Choose original or defining leader recordings where possible. Live room sound is often evidence of the central musical function and should not automatically be replaced by a studio remake.
- Contradiction: A commercial recording can be organized around participation rather than virtuoso display.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
14 selected candidate recordings, with 13 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Maranatha! Music — Seek Ye First: Hear a short repeated melody and round-like potential invite immediate participation. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/seek-ye-first/715701019?i=715703297). Proposed sequence year 1972; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 2. Maranatha! Music — Father I Adore You: Hear a compact phrase become a communal texture through repetition. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/father-i-adore-you/1443850971?i=1443850973). Proposed sequence year 1972; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 3. Jack Hayford — Majesty: Hear a clear rising melody and harmonic arrival enlarge collective address. [Catalog/context](https://www.worshipfuel.com/equip/an-interview-with-modern-day-worship-music-pioneer-don-moen/). Proposed sequence year 1981; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 4. Maranatha! Music — As the Deer: Hear a gentle strophic melody balance personal language and shared singing. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/as-the-deer/1444094383?i=1444094900). Proposed sequence year 1984; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 5. Don Moen — Give Thanks: Hear a leader and room create a continuous, repeatable worship arc. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/give-thanks/1795681796?i=1795681803). Proposed sequence year 1986; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 6. Graham Kendrick — Shine Jesus Shine: Hear a strong refrain carry a congregation beyond a quiet verse. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/shine-jesus-shine/1298142387?i=1298143062). Proposed sequence year 1988; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 7. Lenny LeBlanc — There Is None Like You: Hear a restrained melody make space for a room's sustained singing. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/there-is-none-like-you/1814076578?i=1814076717&uo=4). - 8. Ron Kenoly — Ancient of Days: Hear call, rhythm and ensemble color give communal repetition a more active groove. Proposed sequence year 1992; Original-year hypothesis agrees with official catalog release year; confirm any remaster/remake qualifier before publication.
- 9. Darlene Zschech — Shout to the Lord: Hear a memorable melodic ascent organize a growing live collective sound. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/shout-to-the-lord/1795681635?i=1795681790). Proposed sequence year 1994; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 10. Matt Redman — The Heart of Worship: Hear a deliberately reduced arrangement make the act of participation the song's subject. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/the-heart-of-worship/1867029758?i=1867029759). Proposed sequence year 1999; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 11. Paul Baloche — Open the Eyes of My Heart: Hear a short harmonic loop support repeated intensification. - 12. Tim Hughes — Here I Am to Worship: Hear a verse-refrain design carry quiet attention into a common declaration. Proposed sequence year 2001; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 13. Israel & New Breed — You Are Good: Hear gospel-band propulsion enlarge the same participatory function. Proposed sequence year 2001; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.
- 14. Darlene Zschech — Worthy Is the Lamb: Hear a longer vocal arc remain singable through repetition and cadence. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/worthy-is-the-lamb-feat-svrcina-2024-version/1791326779?i=1791326796). Proposed sequence year 2001; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.

### Inferences
- The sequence is chronological by proposed original/repertoire year, with later interpretations and archive dates distinguished. Each track has a separate listening job.

### Gaps
- Catalog match pending: Jack Hayford - Majesty
- Before publication, confirm exact recording versions and original chronology, then check availability again. Spotify matching and live playlist checks have not been performed.

## What remains before publication?

### Takeaway
No playlist has been created or modified. This research draft is not yet a service-verified publication.

### Cited Findings
- Raw US catalog responses are preserved in `catalog-raw/global-worship.json`; the [Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#worship) supplies genealogy.

### Inferences
- The title and cover concept can be debated independently of remaining catalog repairs.

### Gaps
- Spotify matching, image visual review or production, final original-master checks and publication approval remain.

## Final competition and catalog review

13 retained selections have US catalog title/performer matches. 2 have additional original-album/year metadata support; this does not replace a listening check. 13 are eligible for the future import text. No service publication has occurred.

### Candidate competition
- Solo pop cover singers — Give Thanks virtuosic version: A technically impressive cover can conceal the room's participatory job.
- Hillsong UNITED — Oceans: Reserve the arena/alternative-rock dynamic for Modern Worship.
- Jack Hayford — Majesty: The Jack Hayford recording was not located. A Maranatha! Music interpretation is a different performer/master; keep the repertoire reference without a false original credit.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

PRAISE & WORSHIP · The Chorus Gives the Room a Voice
- Shape: One simple stack of nesting chairs at lower left unfolds into a broad open circle of five chairs; no people, symbols or writing. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#687236), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: praise_worship

classes.researchNotesText:
# Modern Worship

## What musical change should this class reveal?

### Takeaway
Layers, register and dynamics make repeated material feel like development; the congregation becomes part of the arrangement.

### Cited Findings
- The Atlas records the direct links used here: [Music Atlas](https://musicatlas.us/#modernworship).
- Historical/performance context is supported by the [style source](https://hillsong.com/music/worship); this source does not certify every archive master or year in the candidate list.

### Inferences
- Compare the alternative/arena-rock turn, intimate reductions and later gospel-oriented crossings; do not equate one megachurch brand with every congregation or with the whole genre.
- Contradiction: A song designed for mass participation can borrow the production drama of an individual rock performance.

### Gaps
- Precise recording identities remain separately reviewable; see per-track metadata.

## Which recordings make the sequence audible?

### Takeaway
16 selected candidate recordings, with 16 sufficiently close US catalog title/performer matches.

### Cited Findings
- 1. Delirious? — Did You Feel the Mountains Tremble?: Hear a congregational refrain acquire a rock band's dynamic release. [Catalog/context](https://music.apple.com/us/album/did-you-feel-the-mountains-tremble/1818630334?i=1818631689). Proposed sequence year 1994; Proposed original song/release chronology; recording identity and year evidence reviewed separately below.

## Final competition and catalog review

### Candidate competition

Question: How does a band make a room's singing feel larger without adding new words?

Listening revelation: Layers, register and dynamics make repeated material feel like development; the congregation becomes part of the arrangement.

Contradiction: A song designed for mass participation can borrow the production drama of an individual rock performance.

Musical argument: Compare the alternative/arena-rock turn, intimate reductions and later gospel-oriented crossings; do not equate one megachurch brand with every congregation or with the whole genre.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

MODERN WORSHIP · The Room Becomes the Chorus
- Shape: One empty retractable seating bank at lower left unfolds into three broad ascending terraces; a translucent cloth bridges their steps, leaving the upper right empty. Artwork stays in the lower 55%, clear of the subtitle; nothing in the upper right. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#687236), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

# 72.12.1 BANDA · The Brass Band Holds the Conversation

Prepared, unpublished. No service playlist or app link was created.

## Listening lesson

Question: How can a large brass band leave room for a singer's intimate phrasing?

Revelation: Tuba anchors the step while trumpets, clarinets and trombones answer the singer in sharp blocks of sound.

Contradiction: The largest ensemble can make the closest vocal address.

Argument: Tuba anchors the step while trumpets, clarinets and trombones answer the singer in sharp blocks of sound. The largest ensemble can make the closest vocal address. The sequence first establishes the inherited gesture,then makes the defining arrangement audible,and ends with a documented mutation rather than a compulsory recent hit.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

BANDA · The Brass Band Holds the Conversation
- Shape: one small cream speech-shaped cutout set inside three large interlocking brass-colored brackets, with generous dark gaps. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

# 72.14.1 NORTEÑO · The Accordion Answers the Story

Prepared, unpublished. No service playlist or app link was created.

## Listening lesson

Question: How do the voice and accordion divide the telling of a song?

Revelation: Accordion and bajo sexto trade short figures beneath duet singing, with a firm dance pulse carrying romance and narrative.

Contradiction: A dance-band format can carry a complex sequential narrative.

Argument: Accordion and bajo sexto trade short figures beneath duet singing, with a firm dance pulse carrying romance and narrative. A dance-band format can carry a complex sequential narrative. The sequence first establishes the inherited gesture,then makes the defining arrangement audible,and ends with a documented mutation rather than a compulsory recent hit.

Draw this

NORTEÑO · The Accordion Answers the Story
- Shape: two alternating zigzag strips surrounding one straight narrow path, their ends fitting like a conversation. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

## Listening lesson

Question: Which musical parts survive as Tejano changes its instrumentation and audience?

Revelation: Accordion, brass, keyboards and R&B-shaped voices share dance arrangements that move between languages and ensemble traditions.

Contradiction: Crossover can make a local ensemble identity clearer rather than weaker.

Argument: Accordion, brass, keyboards and R&B-shaped voices share dance arrangements that move between languages and ensemble traditions. classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

TEJANO · The Border Band Changes Its Shape
- Shape: four unlike paper tabs meeting in one fitted joint, with each tab retaining its own distinct edge. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
