- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. # 72.12.1.1 TECHNOBANDA · The Dance Band Goes Electric

Prepared, unpublished. No service playlist or app link was created.

## Listening lesson

Question: What happens when electronic instruments take the jobs of a brass band?

Revelation: Keyboards, electric bass and drums reshape banda attack into a clipped, bouncing quebradita pulse.

Contradiction: Smaller forces can make a larger physical dance impulse.

Argument: Keyboards, electric bass and drums reshape banda attack into a clipped, bouncing quebradita pulse. Smaller forces can make a larger physical dance impulse. The sequence first establishes the inherited gesture,then makes the defining arrangement audible,and ends with a documented mutation rather than a compulsory recent hit.

- **Banda Toro — La Noche Que Murió Chicago**: 1993 → 1993. Retain1993 as earliest directly documented circulation, despite the selected carrier’s1994 date. Exact first single day (and any earlier1992 claim) is not established; the chart identifies the period commercial hit, not a later live remake. Sources: [1](https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/90s/1993/BB-1993-10-02.pdf).
- **Banda Maguey — El Teterete**: 1994 → 1995. Banda Maguey’s own discography lists El Teterete on La Estrella de los Bailes, year1995, Fonovisa; its biography explicitly calls that the1995 second album. The exact original-album catalog agrees. Replace the1994 seed, which belongs to the preceding Tumbando Caña stage. Sources: [1](https://www.bandamaguey.com/discografia), [2](https://www.bandamaguey.com/biografia), [3](https://music.apple.com/us/album/la-estrella-de-los-bailes/1772712177).

The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

DURANGUENSE · The Keyboard Keeps the Dance Moving
- Shape: three short rectangular steps repeated beneath one long flowing paper band, its folds falling between the steps. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

## Listening lesson

Question: How much narrative and rhythmic movement can a very small guitar-led band hold?

Revelation: Plucked lead guitar, close singing and a compact bass pulse let a small ensemble carry corridos and intimate romantic songs.

Contradiction: A light instrumental texture can carry a heavy narrative.

Argument: Plucked lead guitar, close singing and a compact bass pulse let a small ensemble carry corridos and intimate romantic songs. A light instrumental texture can carry a heavy narrative. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

ROOTS REGGAE · The Song Holds a Collective Ground
- Shape: three upright folded sheets supporting one broad shared lintel, each sheet a different height but all bearing weight. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F4D36), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

## Listening lesson

Question: What does a deejay add when the backing track is already familiar?

Revelation: Deejays talk, chant and sing over shared rhythm tracks, shifting familiar songs through timing, comic character and public address.

Contradiction: Borrowed accompaniment makes an individual voice more distinctive.

Draw this

TOASTING / DEEJAY · The Speaking Voice Takes the Riddim
- Shape: one long smooth paper ribbon crossed by an irregular chain of small sharply folded tabs. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F4D36), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: toasting_deejay

## Listening lesson

Question: How does changing language change the placement of a voice inside a riddim?

Revelation: Panamanian voices reshape Jamaican dancehall patterns in Spanish, using clipped hooks, local narration and later romantic melody.

Contradiction: Translation becomes a new rhythmic performance.

Argument: Panamanian voices reshape Jamaican dancehall patterns in Spanish, using clipped hooks, local narration and later romantic melody. Translation becomes a new rhythmic performance. classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

REGGAE EN ESPAÑOL · The Riddim Finds Another Language
- Shape: one staggered row of broad blocks whose spacing gradually changes while its outline remains recognizable. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F4D36), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

UNDERGROUND (PUERTO RICO) · The Mixtape Builds a Public
- Shape: many small torn paper rectangles joined into one sturdy strip by visibly overlapping seams. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F4D36), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

LATIN HIP HOP · The Verse Crosses Languages
- Shape: two unequal columns of short paper bars exchanging pieces through one open gap, no maps or flags. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1E1C1A), flat and untinted; title ink (#E8B84A) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #E8B84A, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

## Listening lesson

Question: How many vocal identities can the same recognizable rhythmic skeleton support?

Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F4D36), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

DEMBOW (DOMINICAN) · The Short Hook Drives the Dance
- Shape: one small jagged paper notch repeated across a broad strip, with three shifts of spacing creating visible motion. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F4D36), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

## Listening lesson

Question: How does a rock band make local speech and rhythmic memory part of its sound?

Revelation: Spanish-language voices recast rock riffs, new-wave pulse and local rhythmic memory as distinct songs rather than translations.

Contradiction: A shared language does not make one uniform rock scene.

Argument: Spanish-language voices recast rock riffs, new-wave pulse and local rhythmic memory as distinct songs rather than translations. A shared language does not make one uniform rock scene. classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

ROCK EN ESPAÑOL · The Rock Band Finds Its Own Accent
- Shape: one long cream strip folded into four visibly different corners, all made from the same sheet. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#F1EEE6), flat and untinted; title ink (#28706B) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #28706B, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

# 71.01.1.1.3 SOCAL REGGAE ROCK · The Offbeat Changes the Rock Band

Prepared and unpublished. Chronology refreshed November 14, 2026. No service changes.

## Listening lesson

Question: How does a rock band change when it learns to leave reggae-sized spaces?

Revelation: Reggae space and offbeat guitar meet punk attack, rap phrasing and pop choruses in flexible band arrangements.

Contradiction: A relaxed pocket can hold abrasive voices and sudden force.

Argument: Reggae space and offbeat guitar meet punk attack, rap phrasing and pop choruses in flexible band arrangements. A relaxed pocket can hold abrasive voices and sudden force. The sequence first establishes the inherited gesture,then makes the defining arrangement audible,and ends with a documented mutation rather than a compulsory recent hit.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

SOCAL REGGAE ROCK · The Offbeat Changes the Rock Band
- Shape: one broad angular strip interrupted by three clean empty slots, with a thin soft strip slipping through the openings. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1F4D36), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

# 21.06.1 '90S NEW COUNTRY · The Country Song Fills the Arena

Prepared and unpublished. Chronology refreshed November 14, 2026. No service changes.

## Listening lesson

Question: How does country retain specific stories while scaling up its audience and sound?

Revelation: Country voices, steel guitar and narrative detail meet rock-sized drums, broad hooks and polished radio arrangements.

Contradiction: A huge chorus can begin with a very small remembered detail.

Argument: Country voices, steel guitar and narrative detail meet rock-sized drums, broad hooks and polished radio arrangements. A huge chorus can begin with a very small remembered detail. The sequence first establishes the inherited gesture,then makes the defining arrangement audible,and ends with a documented mutation rather than a compulsory recent hit.

Draw this

'90S NEW COUNTRY · The Country Song Fills the Arena
- Shape: one tiny stitched paper square expanding into a single large folded canopy, with the original seam still visible. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#C9A27E), flat and untinted; title ink (#29251F) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #29251F, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Draw this

FOLK PUNK · The Small Band Becomes a Crowd
- Shape: one small folded paper cup opening along its seams into a broad irregular shared vessel, no hands or people. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1E1C1A), flat and untinted; title ink (#C9C24A) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #C9C24A, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.researchNotesText:
# 45.03.1 G-FUNK (WEST COAST) · The Slow Groove Carries the Street

Prepared November 14, 2026. **Unpublished.** No service playlist has been created or changed. Course number status: proposed. Proposed numbering follows the saved current map and does not assert that every influence is a primary parent.

## 1. What should the listener learn, and how does the history support it?

### Takeaway

Question: How does a slow instrumental groove change the weight of a rap voice? Revelation: Bass, sliding high lines and sung response can generate momentum while the drum pattern stays patient.

### Cited findings

- [Warren G revisits Regulate](https://www.grammy.com/news/warren-g-interview-regulate-g-funk-era-nate-dogg-30th-anniversary/): Participant account identifies Above the Law, Dre, DJ Quik and Warren G as important contributors and describes Nate Dogg’s structural role.
- [Warren G on making Regulate](https://www.nme.com/features/music-interviews/warren-g-g-funk-making-annie-lennox-starstruck-immortal-regulate-2352168): Participant account of the recording and narrative setting.

Direct connection data: [current Music Atlas map](https://musicatlas.us/musicatlas.json), locally snapshotted as `atlas.json`. Parents: gangsta, pfunk. Children: hyphy. These are the app’s connection claims, not an assertion that music has only these influences.

### Inferences

Musical argument: G-funk is a relationship among pocket, melodic counterline and the voice, not one producer’s invention or a single sampled record. Contradiction: Relaxed musical surfaces can carry tense, specific street narratives. The track jobs below are curatorial listening judgments rather than claims quoted from a source. 

### Gaps

Historical chronology is stored as `originalYear`, separately from the current catalog issue date. For reused Chicago House drafts, original-year claims are carried forward from the identified previous research/version-review files; today’s catalog lookup verifies recording metadata and US streamability, not every historical date independently. New selections combine participant/label sources and the exact catalog carriers; explicit residual chronology questions are retained below.

## 2. Which recordings won the comparison, and why?

### Takeaway

The ready sequence contains 16 recordings. No minimum length was enforced. Repeated artists remain only where their tracks demonstrate distinct development, production or song functions.

### Cited findings

- 1. Above the Law — Murder Rap (1990): An early heavy funk construction sets up the later relaxed synthesis. Carrier: Livin' Like Hustlers; catalog issue 1990-02-08. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/murder-rap/193866697?i=193866772&uo=4).
- 2. DJ Quik — Tonite (1991): Bright keyboard detail and a buoyant pocket establish an independent West Coast route. Carrier: Quik Is the Name; catalog issue 1991-01-15. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/tonite/283661311?i=283661313&uo=4).
- 3. Above the Law — Call It What U Want (1992): High melodic lines and a deep groove move toward the defining sound. Carrier: A Rap Collection; catalog issue 2001-03-13. Original1992single performance on an archival collection, before BlackMafiaLife1993. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/call-it-what-u-want/268498138?i=268498817&uo=4).
- 4. Dr. Dre & Snoop Dogg — Nuthin' But A "G" Thang (1992): A clean instrumental pocket lets two rap voices trade conversational timing. Carrier: The Chronic; catalog issue 1992-11-19. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/nuthin-but-a-g-thang/1668460963?i=1668461604&uo=4).
- 5. Snoop Dogg — Gin and Juice (1993): The laid-back voice becomes inseparable from the bass and refrain. Carrier: Doggystyle; catalog issue 1993-11-23. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/gin-and-juice/1676306182?i=1676306185&uo=4).
- 6. Above the Law — Black Superman (1994): Darker harmonic color broadens the vocabulary beyond sunny ease. Carrier: Uncle Sam's Curse; catalog issue 1994-07-12. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/black-superman/1504066813?i=1504067207&uo=4).
- 7. Warren G — Regulate (feat. Nate Dogg) (1994): Sung narration and rap become equal parts of one story. Carrier: Regulate… G Funk Era; catalog issue 1994-03-22. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/regulate-feat-nate-dogg/1452811329?i=1452811341&uo=4).
- 8. DJ Quik — Dollaz + Sense (1994): Instrumental polish sharpens rather than softens a confrontational performance. Carrier: The Best of DJ Quik - Da Finale; catalog issue 1994-10-14. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/dollaz-sense/255285089?i=255285680&uo=4).
- 9. Twinz — Round & Round (1995): A close vocal blend and rounded bass make the hook part of the pocket. Carrier: Hip-Hop Legacy, Vol. 8; catalog issue 1995-01-01. Original1995recording on an archival HipHopLegacycollection; sameartist and full3:41master retained. Original album carrier remains preferred if available at publication. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/round-round/1031068618?i=1031068688&uo=4).
- 10. The Dove Shack — Summertime In the LBC (1995): A soul-led group turns place into melodic atmosphere. Carrier: This Is the Shack; catalog issue 1995-08-22. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/summertime-in-the-lbc/1443256485?i=1443256501&uo=4).

Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/i-got-5-on-it-feat-michael-marshall/712330598?i=712330693&uo=4).
- 12. Mack 10 — Foe Life (1995): A more forceful voice works against the same unhurried instrumental scale. Carrier: Mack 10; catalog issue 1995-05-26. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/foe-life/723797254?i=723797470&uo=4).
- 13. Nate Dogg — Nobody Does It Better (feat. Warren G) [Original Maxi Version] (1998): The hook singer becomes the organizing lead rather than an embellishment. Carrier: Nobody Does It Better (feat. Warren G); catalog issue 1998-06-23. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/nobody-does-it-better-feat-warren-g-original-maxi-version/350387893?i=350387970&uo=4).
- 14. Xzibit — X (2000): A tighter drum and bass frame carries the vocabulary into a new decade. Carrier: Restless; catalog issue 2000-12-12. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/x/267921139?i=267921364&uo=4).
- 15. Snoop Dogg featuring Akon — Boss' Life (feat. Akon) (2006): Gospel-inflected support expands the voice-and-groove relationship. Carrier: Tha Blue Carpet Treatment; catalog issue 2006-11-21. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/boss-life-feat-akon/1443117112?i=1443117350&uo=4).
- 16. G Perico — All Blue (2017): A younger narrator keeps the conversational pocket while changing its street detail. Carrier: All Blue; catalog issue 2017-04-19. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/all-blue/1723236084?i=1723236086&uo=4).

### Inferences

- Parliament — Flash Light: A vital ancestry comparison; the class gives most space to the rap transformation rather than replaying the funk parent.
- 2Pac — California Love: Importantcrossover, but its maximal chorus would duplicate the anthem lesson and displace independent producer routes.

### Gaps

No essential off-platform candidate is required to complete the verified sequence. Wider scene coverage remains possible; this is a bounded listening argument rather than a comprehensive discography.

## 3. Is this ready for a later publishing batch?

### Takeaway

Every track in `tracks` has an exact official Apple US catalog ID, a returned `isStreamable: true` flag and a current November 14, 2026 check. Raw response paths are stored per track. G-FUNK (WEST COAST) · The Slow Groove Carries the Street
- Shape: A low rounded band supports a narrow wandering line that slides above it, while two short blocks stay evenly spaced below. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1E1C1A), flat and untinted; title ink (#E8B84A) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #E8B84A, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.

# 45.08.2.1 HORRORCORE · The Voice Builds a Nightmare

Prepared November 14, 2026. **Unpublished.** No service playlist has been created or changed. Course number status: proposed. Proposed numbering follows the saved current map and does not assert that every influence is a primary parent.

## 1. What should the listener learn, and how does the history support it?

### Takeaway

Question: How do a voice and a loop make a story feel unsafe before its plot is understood? Revelation: Vocal character, negative space and timbral contrast create horror as strongly as graphic words.

### Cited findings

- [Contemporary CMJ review of6Feet Deep](https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/CMJ/1994/CMJ-New-Music-Report-1994-08-22.pdf): Contemporaneous review stresses Prince Paul’s production as well as the horror imagery.
- [Prince Paul lecture archive](https://www.redbullmusicacademy.com/lectures/prince-paul/): Producer’s own discussion of character, humor and composition provides a research feed; verify relevant recording claims separately.
- [Sub Pop artist catalog: clipping.](https://www.subpop.com/artists/clipping): Official release context for the later experimental horror albums.

Direct connection data: [current Music Atlas map](https://musicatlas.us/musicatlas.json), locally snapshotted as `atlas.json`. Parents: hardcore_hh. Children: trap_metal. These are the app’s connection claims, not an assertion that music has only these influences.

### Inferences

Musical argument: Horrorcore has several musical methods: slow dread, shock theater, rapid character switches and later experimental sound design. Contradiction: Grotesque exaggeration can expose anxiety or social satire rather than simply celebrate violence. The track jobs below are curatorial listening judgments rather than claims quoted from a source. 

### Gaps

Historical chronology is stored as `originalYear`, separately from the current catalog issue date. For reused Chicago House drafts, original-year claims are carried forward from the identified previous research/version-review files; today’s catalog lookup verifies recording metadata and US streamability, not every historical date independently. New selections combine participant/label sources and the exact catalog carriers; explicit residual chronology questions are retained below.

## 2. Which recordings won the comparison, and why?

### Takeaway

The ready sequence contains 16 recordings. No minimum length was enforced. Repeated artists remain only where their tracks demonstrate distinct development, production or song functions.

### Cited findings

- 1. Geto Boys — Mind of a Lunatic (1989): A dislocated narrator and heavy loop turn a rap scene into psychological horror. Carrier: Grip It on That Other Level; catalog issue 1989-03-12. Original1989GripIt recording selected, not the different1990TheGetoBoysalbumtake. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/mind-of-a-lunatic/1812969997?i=1812970157&uo=4).
- 2. Ganksta Nip — Horror Movie Rap (1992): Exaggerated imagery becomes a theatrical vocal method. Carrier: The South Park Psycho; catalog issue 1992-07-01. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/horror-movie-rap/1169323124?i=1169323128&uo=4).
- 3. Brotha Lynch Hung — 24 Deep (1993): A restrained pocket makes the narrator’s extreme detail more unsettling. Carrier: The Ripgut Collection; catalog issue 1993-01-01. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/24-deep/1626318522?i=1626318527&uo=4).
- 4. Esham — The Wicketshit Will Never Die (1994): A harsh and claustrophobic Detroit sound makes the narrator’s world unstable. Carrier: Closed Casket; catalog issue 1994-11-22. KKKilltheFetuswas not resolved inAppleUS. Selected1994TheWicketshitWillNeverDie as a different, verified composition; not a renamed substitute. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/the-wicketshit-will-never-die/276970602?i=276971095&uo=4).

- Type: #E8B84A, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.

# 45.18.1 MAFIOSO RAP · The Verse Becomes a Crime Film

Prepared November 14, 2026. **Unpublished.** No service playlist has been created or changed. Course number status: proposed. Proposed numbering follows the saved current map and does not assert that every influence is a primary parent.

## 1. What should the listener learn, and how does the history support it?

### Takeaway

Question: How can a rap verse create an ensemble crime film without a screen? Revelation: Specific objects, compressed dialogue and changes in point of view make the beat feel like a scene.

### Cited findings

- [Raekwon and collaborators on making Only Built4Cuban Linx](https://www.xxlmag.com/raekwon-the-making-of-only-built-for-cuban-linx/): Participant recollections locate the1995recording among earlier Kool G Rap and Mob Style work.
- [Wu-Tang Clan lecture on Cuban Linx and Wu language](https://www.redbullmusicacademy.com/lectures/wu-tang-lecture/): Primary group discussion of the narrative recording and shared vocabulary.
- [Raekwon20th-anniversary interview](https://www.spinmagazine.com/2015/07/raekwon-only-built-4-cuban-linx-20th-anniversary-interview/): Participant explanation of the album’s filmmaking and scene-setting methods.

Direct connection data: [current Music Atlas map](https://musicatlas.us/musicatlas.json), locally snapshotted as `atlas.json`. Parents: boombap, gangsta. Children: none in this map. These are the app’s connection claims, not an assertion that music has only these influences.

### Inferences

Musical argument: Mafioso rap is a narrative and production practice: persona, setting and consequence matter more than references to mob films alone. Contradiction: The narrator can sound powerful while the story reveals how precarious that power is. The track jobs below are curatorial listening judgments rather than claims quoted from a source. 

### Gaps

Historical chronology is stored as `originalYear`, separately from the current catalog issue date. For reused Chicago House drafts, original-year claims are carried forward from the identified previous research/version-review files; today’s catalog lookup verifies recording metadata and US streamability, not every historical date independently. New selections combine participant/label sources and the exact catalog carriers; explicit residual chronology questions are retained below.

## 2. Which recordings won the comparison, and why?

### Takeaway

The ready sequence contains 16 recordings. No minimum length was enforced. Repeated artists remain only where their tracks demonstrate distinct development, production or song functions.

### Cited findings

- 1. Kool G Rap — ILL Street Blues (1992): Close narrative detail and a hard loop turn street description into a scene. Carrier: The Pre-Kill, Vol. 2; catalog issue 1992-11-17. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/ill-street-blues/535306790?i=535307468&uo=4).
- 2. Raekwon — Criminology (feat. Ghostface Killah) (1995): Urgent exchanges and film-like framing establish the ensemble world. Carrier: Only Built 4 Cuban Linx...; catalog issue 1995-06-26. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/criminology-feat-ghostface-killah/258634938?i=258635309&uo=4).
- 3. Raekwon — Glaciers of Ice (feat. Ghostface Killah & Masta Killa) (1995): Voices and luxury detail thicken the imagined setting rather than repeating a simple hook. Carrier: Only Built 4 Cuban Linx...; catalog issue 1995-08-01. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/glaciers-of-ice-feat-ghostface-killah-masta-killa/258634938?i=258636970&uo=4).
- 4. AZ — Sugar Hill (1995): A smooth sung surface contrasts with the narrator’s account of aspiration and risk. Carrier: Doe or Die; catalog issue 1995-10-10. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/sugar-hill/724052211?i=724052404&uo=4).
- 5. Kool G Rap — Fast Life (1995): A polished duet connects the pioneer to a younger narrative generation. Carrier: 4, 5, 6; catalog issue 1995-09-26. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/fast-life/169715139?i=169715616&uo=4).
- 6. Mobb Deep featuring Nas — Eye for a Eye (Your Beef Is Mines) [feat. Nas & Raekwon The Chef] (1995): A stark loop lets guest voices inhabit the same threatening space. Carrier: The Infamous; catalog issue 1995-04-25. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/eye-for-a-eye-your-beef-is-mines-feat-nas-raekwon-the-chef/255342338?i=255342955&uo=4).
- 7. JAŸ-Z — Dead Presidents II (1996): Understatement and moral calculation replace a purely triumphant persona. Carrier: Reasonable Doubt; catalog issue 1996-06-25. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/dead-presidents-ii/1475940563?i=1475940807&uo=4).
- 8. Nas — The Message (1996): String-like texture and a controlled voice make narrative authority cinematic. Carrier: It Was Written; catalog issue 1996-07-02. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/the-message/211507540?i=211507693&uo=4).
- 9. Lil' Kim — Queen Bitch (1996): A woman claims the authoritative crime persona rather than merely serving its story. Carrier: Hard Core; catalog issue 1996-11-12. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/queen-bitch/321976585?i=321976619&uo=4).
- 10. AZ, Nas, Nature & Dr. Dre — Phone Tap (Explicit) (1997): Telephone framing makes surveillance and dialogue part of the arrangement. Carrier: The Album; catalog issue 1997-10-21. The Firm group is cataloged under its performing members AZ,Nas,Nature&Dr.Dre; exactoriginalalbumrecording selected. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/phone-tap-explicit/1428753075?i=1428754755&uo=4).
- 11. The Notorious B.I.G. — N****s Bleed (2007 Remaster) (1997): Extended narration makes small turns of plot carry musical suspense. Carrier: Greatest Hits; catalog issue 1997-03-25. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/n-s-bleed-2007-remaster/216666654?i=216666936&uo=4).
- 12. Ghostface Killah — Shakey Dog (Explicit) (2006): Dense sensory detail and sudden shifts make the older method newly frantic. Carrier: Fishscale (Expanded Edition); catalog issue 2006-03-28. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/shakey-dog-explicit/1471570992?i=1471570996&uo=4).
- 13. Raekwon — Cold Outside (feat. Ghostface Killah & Sugar Bang) (2009): The returning narrator makes consequences and regret part of the film. Carrier: Only Built 4 Cuban Linx, Pt. 2; catalog issue 2009-09-07. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/cold-outside-feat-ghostface-killah-sugar-bang/716639724?i=716639824&uo=4).
- 14. Roc Marciano — Snow (2010): A reduced instrumental frame gives compressed imagery exceptional weight. Carrier: Marcberg Deluxe; catalog issue 2010-05-04. Corrected seed’s erroneous2013date. Artistinterview and originalalbumcredit place the recording in2010. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/snow/1823170250?i=1823170411&uo=4).
- 15. Westside Gunn — Elizabeth (2018): An understated loop and distinctive vocal texture renew the luxury-and-threat persona. Carrier: Supreme Blientele; catalog issue 2018-06-22. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/elizabeth/1604969509?i=1604970227&uo=4).
- 16. Freddie Gibbs, The Alchemist & Rick Ross — Scottie Beam (2020): A modern storyteller combines social observation, risk and cinematic detail. Carrier: Alfredo; catalog issue 2020-05-29. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/scottie-beam/1513978902?i=1513978905&uo=4).

### Inferences

- Nas — The World Is Yours: Broader reflective rap rather than the more specific crime-film method taught here.
- Rick Ross — B.M.F.: A strong later persona, but this class prioritizes detailed narrative construction over slogan-scale grandeur.

### Gaps

- Kool G Rap & DJ Polo — Road to the Riches: Noexactartist/title/versionmatchedthecatalogquery.

## 3. Is this ready for a later publishing batch?

### Takeaway

Every track in `tracks` has an exact official Apple US catalog ID, a returned `isStreamable: true` flag and a current November 14, 2026 check. Raw response paths are stored per track. All are explicitly import-eligible; off-platform candidates are kept outside this list. Spotify matching has **not** been checked and remains a prepublication step.

### Cited findings

The class JSON stores the ID, full URL, catalog title/artist, carrier album, duration, release date and ISRC where returned, plus the raw lookup file. US lookup responses live in `catalog-electronic/`. The current snapshot establishes availability at check time, not a guarantee of future availability. Cover art is a prepared prompt and expected file path, with existence checked separately; no new cover was generated.

### Inferences

Publish Apple Music first only after the remaining edition/chronology questions are resolved or explicitly accepted. Check the actual imported identities, chronology and public sharing, then copy that verified sequence to Spotify and check its matches. Generate the app manifest only after actual public URLs exist. Current draft URLs are catalog songs, never invented public playlist links.

- 1researchedcandidatesremainoffplatformorunresolved; noneareincludedintheverifiedimportsequence.
- Spotify destination matching, service order verification and public playlist URLs are pending.
- No authorization to publish is implied by this research preparation.

MAFIOSO RAP · The Verse Becomes a Crime Film
- Shape: Three overlapping strips of paper each contain one empty rectangular window; their windows align into a single deep corridor while the paper edges suggest edits. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1E1C1A), flat and untinted; title ink (#E8B84A) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #E8B84A, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.
