classes.researchNotesText:
# 45.04.4 CHOPPED AND SCREWED · Slowed Time Changes the Voice

Prepared November 14, 2026. **Unpublished.** No service playlist has been created or changed. Course number status: proposed. Proposed numbering follows the saved current map and does not assert that every influence is a primary parent.

## 1. What should the listener learn, and how does the history support it?

### Takeaway

Question: What changes in a rap performance when time, pitch and repetition are treated as compositional controls? Revelation: A vocal phrase can acquire new weight and meaning when its pitch drops and a fragment returns before the sentence moves on.

### Cited findings

- [Texas State Historical Association: rap and hip-hop](https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/rap-and-hip-hop): Historical account of DJ Screw’s slowed tempos, repeated phrases and local tape circulation.
- [University of Houston DJ Screw Papers finding aid](https://txarchives.org/uhsc/finding_aids/00113.xml): Primary archive context for personalized tapes, local rappers and the spread of the technique.
- [Resident Advisor history with Lance Scott Walker and Rabit](https://ra.co/features/4040): Track-led research feed connecting Screw’s practice to later music; full article body was not available in browser text.
- [DJ Screw — Tell Me Something Good, official artist channel / Virgin delivery](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uFsmqGl0u9w): Label-delivered metadata names All Screwed Up,Vol.2, ℗1995 Bigtyme/SoSouth and release August1,1995.

Direct connection data: [current Music Atlas map](https://musicatlas.us/musicatlas.json), locally snapshotted as `atlas.json`. Parents: southern_hh. Children: witchhouse. These are the app’s connection claims, not an assertion that music has only these influences.

### Inferences

Musical argument: Chopping and slowing are separate operations whose combination produces the distinctive suspended Houston groove. Contradiction: Manipulating an existing performance creates a new expressive recording rather than simply a slower playback. The track jobs below are curatorial listening judgments rather than claims quoted from a source. 

### Gaps

Historical chronology is stored as `originalYear`, separately from the current catalog issue date. For reused Chicago House drafts, original-year claims are carried forward from the identified previous research/version-review files; today’s catalog lookup verifies recording metadata and US streamability, not every historical date independently. New selections combine participant/label sources and the exact catalog carriers; explicit residual chronology questions are retained below.

## 2. Which recordings won the comparison, and why?

### Takeaway

The ready sequence contains 7 recordings. No minimum length was enforced. Repeated artists remain only where their tracks demonstrate distinct development, production or song functions.

### Cited findings

- 1. DJ Screw & Point Blank — My Mind Went Blank (Screwed) (1995): A lowered and repeated voice makes the narrator sound suspended inside the beat. Carrier: All Screwed Up, Vol. 2 (Screwed); catalog issue 1995-08-01. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/my-mind-went-blank-screwed/1872940823?i=1872941058&uo=4).
- 2. DJ Screw & Lil' Keke — Pimp Tha Pen (Screwed) (1995): A local freestyle shows how slowed time changes the rapper’s rhythmic presence. Carrier: 3 'N The Mornin’ Part Two (Screwed); catalog issue 1995-09-26. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/pimp-tha-pen-screwed/1851163385?i=1851163706&uo=4).
- 3. DJ Screw — Tell Me Something Good (Screwed) [feat. UGK] (1995): A soul-derived source makes the altered time expressive beyond a rapfreestyle. Carrier: Banging (Screwed); catalog issue 1995-08-01. The1995 commercial Screw treatment is the teaching object, carried on the later Banging archive. Official label-delivered artist-channel metadata dates All Screwed Up,Vol.2 to August1,1995. Do not present the2018 archive date as the performance year or claim an earlier private tape origin. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/tell-me-something-good-screwed-feat-ugk/1857929336?i=1857929792&uo=4).
- 4. Mike Jones — Still Tippin' (2005): A commercially prominent Houston track carries the local method toward a wider audience. Carrier: Who Is Mike Jones? Screwed & Chopped; catalog issue 2005-04-19. SelectedChopped&Screwedalbumissued2005; theunprocessed2004singleyearisnotusedfortheversion. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/still-tippin/59423155?i=59423111&uo=4).
- 5. Paul Wall — Sittin' Sidewayz (Featuring Big Pokey) (2005): A polished album single remains responsive to the altered-time practice. Carrier: The People's Champ (Chopped & Screwed); catalog issue 2005-07-19. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/sittin-sidewayz-featuring-big-pokey/80430994?i=80430500&uo=4).
- 6. A$AP Rocky — Purple Swag (2011): A descendant comparison places lowered vocal color inside a new original production rather than a complete Screw treatment. Carrier: LIVE.LOVE.A$AP; catalog issue 2011-10-31. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/purple-swag/1591647717?i=1591648347&uo=4).
- 7. Don Toliver — No Idea (CHOPNOTSLOP REMIX) (2020): An official later treatment joins melodic rap to the inherited Houston method. Carrier: Heaven Or Hell (CHOPNOTSLOP REMIX); catalog issue 2020-04-17. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/no-idea-chopnotslop-remix/1508226889?i=1508227386&uo=4).

### Inferences

- The Weeknd — Wicked Games (ChoppedNotSlopped): Influential fan-mixtape circulation, but no verified licensedcatalog edition yet.
- DJ Screw — Tell Me Something Good: Considered for the tape vocabulary; the finaldraft reserves room for the long socialform of June27th.

- UGK — Int'l Players Anthem (I Choose You) (Chopped&Screwed): Matcherreturnedregular2007albumrecording, notthechoppedversion.

## 3. Is this ready for a later publishing batch?

### Takeaway

Every track in `tracks` has an exact official Apple US catalog ID, a returned `isStreamable: true` flag and a current November 14, 2026 check. Raw response paths are stored per track. All are explicitly import-eligible; off-platform candidates are kept outside this list. Spotify matching has **not** been checked and remains a prepublication step.

### Cited findings

The class JSON stores the ID, full URL, catalog title/artist, carrier album, duration, release date and ISRC where returned, plus the raw lookup file. US lookup responses live in `catalog-electronic/`. The current snapshot establishes availability at check time, not a guarantee of future availability. Cover art is a prepared prompt and expected file path, with existence checked separately; no new cover was generated.

### Inferences

Publish Apple Music first only after the remaining edition/chronology questions are resolved or explicitly accepted. Check the actual imported identities, chronology and public sharing, then copy that verified sequence to Spotify and check its matches. Generate the app manifest only after actual public URLs exist. Current draft URLs are catalog songs, never invented public playlist links.

### Gaps

- 4researchedcandidatesremainoffplatformorunresolved; noneareincludedintheverifiedimportsequence.
- Spotify destination matching, service order verification and public playlist URLs are pending.
- No authorization to publish is implied by this research preparation.

CHOPPED AND SCREWED · Slowed Time Changes the Voice
- Shape: A long printed strip passes under a broad transparent weight; its marks widen and several segments double back across themselves before continuing. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1E1C1A), flat and untinted; title ink (#E8B84A) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #E8B84A, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.researchNotesText:
# 41.04.1 HIP HOP SOUL · The Singer Lives Inside the Break

Prepared November 14, 2026. **Unpublished.** No service playlist has been created or changed. Course number status: proposed. Proposed numbering follows the saved current map and does not assert that every influence is a primary parent.

## 1. What should the listener learn, and how does the history support it?

### Takeaway

Question: What changes when a soul singer phrases as though the rap beat belongs to the voice? Revelation: A repeated break becomes expressive support for breaths, rough edges, conversational rhythm and a sung refrain.

### Cited findings

- [Library of Congress My Life essay](https://www.loc.gov/static/programs/national-recording-preservation-board/documents/My-Life_Alexander.pdf): Blige’s1992debut and1994follow-up are central to the hip-hop-soul shift.
- [Producer Chucky Thompson on My Life](https://www.grammy.com/news/producer-chucky-thompson-revisits-25th-anniversary-mary-j-blige-my-life-interview/): Producer testimony on the1994recording, sample vocabulary and vocal approach.
- [Mary J. Blige interview](https://www.xxlmag.com/mary-j-blige-something-bout-myself-excerpt-from-the-november-2011-issue/): Blige describes the shift from new jack swing to hip-hop soul.

Direct connection data: [current Music Atlas map](https://musicatlas.us/musicatlas.json), locally snapshotted as `atlas.json`. Parents: njs, boombap. Children: neosoul. These are the app’s connection claims, not an assertion that music has only these influences.

### Inferences

Musical argument: Hip hop soul changes the relationship between the singer and the beat, beyond simply adding a guest rapper. Contradiction: A fixed sampled groove can make a highly individual live voice feel more immediate. The track jobs below are curatorial listening judgments rather than claims quoted from a source. 

### Gaps

Historical chronology is stored as `originalYear`, separately from the current catalog issue date. For reused Chicago House drafts, original-year claims are carried forward from the identified previous research/version-review files; today’s catalog lookup verifies recording metadata and US streamability, not every historical date independently. New selections combine participant/label sources and the exact catalog carriers; explicit residual chronology questions are retained below.

## 2. Which recordings won the comparison, and why?

### Takeaway

The ready sequence contains 16 recordings. No minimum length was enforced. Repeated artists remain only where their tracks demonstrate distinct development, production or song functions.

### Cited findings

- 1. Mary J. Blige — Real Love (1992): A recognizable break holds a rough and direct soul lead. Carrier: What's The 411?; catalog issue 1992-07-28. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/real-love/1440817005?i=1440817021&uo=4).
- 2. Jodeci — Come & Talk To Me (feat. Fat Doug) [Hip Hop Remix] (1992): A remix recasts an existing vocal through the rap producer’s drum language. Carrier: Forever My Lady (Expanded Edition); catalog issue 1991-05-28. 1992HipHopRemix withFatDoug intentionally selected on expanded1991album; do not sequence it as1991just because the album has that date. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/come-talk-to-me-feat-fat-doug-hip-hop-remix/1609528635?i=1609529183&uo=4).
- 3. SWV — Right Here (Human Nature Radio Mix) (1993): A familiar sample becomes the harmonic frame for vocal group interplay. Carrier: It's About Time; catalog issue 1992-10-27. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/right-here-human-nature-radio-mix/266799911?i=266800348&uo=4).
- 4. Mary J. Blige — My Life (1994): Longer phrases and vulnerable timbre turn a loop into an intimate emotional space. Carrier: My Life (Bonus Track Version); catalog issue 1994-11-29. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/my-life/1440837272?i=1440838052&uo=4).
- 5. Faith Evans — You Used to Love Me (1995): Gospel-derived detail works inside clipped drums rather than above them. Carrier: Faith; catalog issue 1995-07-13. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/you-used-to-love-me/78988685?i=78988675&uo=4).
- 6. Total — Can't You See (feat. The Notorious B.I.G.) (1995): A group lead and rap feature inhabit one beat rather than alternating genres. Carrier: Can't You See (The Remixes) - EP; catalog issue 1995-01-01. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/cant-you-see-feat-the-notorious-b-i-g/1604628543?i=1604628729&uo=4).

- 11. Blackstreet — No Diggity (feat. Dr. Dre & Queen Pen) (1996): A repeating keyboard figure becomes a meeting point for singing and rap. Carrier: Another Level; catalog issue 1996-07-29. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/no-diggity-feat-dr-dre-queen-pen/1440908643?i=1440908981&uo=4).
- 12. Erykah Badu — On & On (1996): A deliberately relaxed placement points toward neo soul without losing the break. Carrier: Baduizm; catalog issue 1996-12-10. Single first issuedDecember1996beforeBaduizm1997. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/on-on/1440837269?i=1440837273&uo=4).
- 13. Alicia Keys — Fallin' (2001): Piano and gospel tension enter the established drum-centered frame. Carrier: Songs In A Minor; catalog issue 2001-03-28. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/fallin/256936779?i=256937038&uo=4).
- 14. Beyoncé — Crazy in Love (feat. JAŸ-Z) (2003): A sharp horn loop lets singing and rhythmic speech exchange force. Carrier: Dangerously in Love; catalog issue 2003-05-14. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/crazy-in-love-feat-ja%C3%BF-z/201274359?i=201274644&uo=4).
- 15. Amerie — 1 Thing (2005): A busy sampled drum break makes the singer’s repeated phrase a rhythmic event. Carrier: Touch; catalog issue 2005-01-05. Original soloalbum version, not the Evebonusmix. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/1-thing/153437601?i=153437689&uo=4).
- 16. Kehlani — CRZY (2016): A later singer turns clipped phrasing and a hard contemporary beat into assertive pop. Carrier: SweetSexySavage (Deluxe); catalog issue 2016-07-15. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/crzy/1192528158?i=1192528515&uo=4).

### Inferences

- Mary J. Blige — You Remind Me: Strong debut choice; Real Love more directly exposes the break, while My Life earns the development slot.
- SZA — The Weekend: Related laterR&B, but including it would weaken the lesson’s specific break-led rhythmic thread.

### Gaps

No essential off-platform candidate is required to complete the verified sequence. Wider scene coverage remains possible; this is a bounded listening argument rather than a comprehensive discography.

- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. classes.description: 1991–present: Fast repeated breaks, shouted calls and clipped replies make the audience part of the beat. Local names, dance commands and queer performance voices keep the groove communal. FROM: Miami Bass. LED TO: Milwaukee Lowend.
classes.listeningQuestion: How can a repeated beat turn a room of dancers into part of the arrangement?
classes.revelation: The caller’s pauses and commands leave slots for the audience; the response is a structural part of the music.
classes.contradiction: A highly local set of names and gestures can travel widely while remaining rooted in community participation.
classes.musicalArgument: Bounce is a call-and-response performance practice, not simply a tempo, bass sample or isolated twerking cue.

classes.researchNotesText:
# 80.07.1.2 BOUNCE · The Call Turns the Room into a Chorus

Prepared November 14, 2026. **Unpublished.** No service playlist has been created or changed. Course number status: proposed. Proposed numbering follows the saved current map and does not assert that every influence is a primary parent.

## 1. What should the listener learn, and how does the history support it?

### Takeaway

Question: How can a repeated beat turn a room of dancers into part of the arrangement? Revelation: The caller’s pauses and commands leave slots for the audience; the response is a structural part of the music.

### Cited findings

- [New Orleans cultural history: bounce](https://www.neworleans.com/things-to-do/music/history-and-traditions/new-orleans-bounce-music/): Local cultural account identifies foundational artists and dance-centered participation.

# 44.01.1.4.2 BEATDOWN HARDCORE · The Pause Becomes the Heavy Part

Prepared and unpublished. Chronology refreshed November 14, 2026. No service changes.

## Listening lesson

Question: How does slowing and interrupting the riff change the crowd's bodily response?

Revelation: Half-time riffs, low guitar and shouted cues make stops and breakdowns into the center of hardcore movement.

Contradiction: The empty interval can feel heavier than the sounding chord.

Argument: Half-time riffs, low guitar and shouted cues make stops and breakdowns into the center of hardcore movement. The empty interval can feel heavier than the sounding chord. The sequence first establishes the inherited gesture,then makes the defining arrangement audible,and ends with a documented mutation rather than a compulsory recent hit.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

BEATDOWN HARDCORE · The Pause Becomes the Heavy Part
- Shape: two massive near-touching rectangular slabs separated by one very narrow cream gap, one tiny wedge inside the gap. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1E1C1A), flat and untinted; title ink (#C9C24A) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #C9C24A, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Prepared and unpublished. Chronology refreshed November 14, 2026. No service changes.

## Listening lesson

Question: How does exaggeration change the emotional range of heavy music?

Revelation: Shrieks, abrupt cuts and exaggerated rhythmic gestures pull hardcore toward theatrical exchange, unstable groove and sudden melody.

Contradiction: Comedy and menace can coexist inside the same precise gesture.

Argument: Shrieks, abrupt cuts and exaggerated rhythmic gestures pull hardcore toward theatrical exchange, unstable groove and sudden melody. Comedy and menace can coexist inside the same precise gesture. The sequence first establishes the inherited gesture,then makes the defining arrangement audible,and ends with a documented mutation rather than a compulsory recent hit.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

SASSCORE · The Heavy Voice Refuses a Straight Face
- Shape: one severe rectangular paper form splitting open to reveal an off-center serrated curl, no face or symbols. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#1E1C1A), flat and untinted; title ink (#C9C24A) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #C9C24A, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: sasscore

Draw this

CASCADIAN BLACK METAL · The Riff Becomes a Place to Stay
- Shape: one stack of rough narrow paper strata opening into a single deep empty cleft, no mountains or trees. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#0E0D0C), flat and untinted; title ink (#D63A2F) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #D63A2F, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

# 43.12.2 NU METALCORE · The Breakdown Learns to Bounce

Prepared and unpublished. Chronology refreshed November 14, 2026. No service changes.

## Listening lesson

Question: What changes when a breakdown gets a nu-metal bounce?

Revelation: Low, syncopated riffs meet metalcore stops, strained vocal characters and electronic interruptions.

Contradiction: Rigid impact gains an elastic bodily swing.

Argument: Low, syncopated riffs meet metalcore stops, strained vocal characters and electronic interruptions. Rigid impact gains an elastic bodily swing. The sequence first establishes the inherited gesture,then makes the defining arrangement audible,and ends with a documented mutation rather than a compulsory recent hit.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

NU METALCORE · The Breakdown Learns to Bounce
- Shape: one heavy rectangular block bending at two soft joints while three smaller blocks hold a straight line. Use the lower55% of a square canvas, leaving clear space beneath the subtitle. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#0E0D0C), flat and untinted; title ink (#D63A2F) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #D63A2F, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: nu_metalcore

classes.researchNotesText:
# 80.01.1.2 DUNGEON SYNTH · A Small Keyboard Builds a World

Prepared November 14, 2026. **Unpublished.** No service playlist has been created or changed. Course number status: proposed. Proposed numbering follows the saved current map and does not assert that every influence is a primary parent.

## 1. What should the listener learn, and how does the history support it?

### Takeaway

Question: How can limited synthetic voices suggest a world larger than their means? Revelation: Repetition and acoustic distance transform cheap timbres into an imagined architecture.

### Cited findings

- [Recording Academy scene report with Mortiis and younger makers](https://www.grammy.com/news/dungeon-synth-scene-report-mortiis-fen-walker-siege-malfet-black-metal/): Mortiis began recording in1993; the2010s revival expanded the atmosphere and social scene. The video-game comparison is embraced by some younger artists but rejected by Mortiis.
- [Community historical guide to dungeon synth](https://dungeon-synth.neocities.org/history): Useful guide to early and revival recordings; terminology is retrospective and should not be imposed as contemporaneous self-identification.
- [Fief — I, artist release page](https://fief.bandcamp.com/album/i): Cobblestone & Magic appears on I, released August1,2016.
- [Fogweaver — Magelight, artist release page](https://thefogweaver.bandcamp.com/album/magelight): Released January13,2023; composition and mastering credits. Corrects provisional2022 dating.
- [Old Tower — The Rise of the Specter part I](https://oldtower.bandcamp.com/track/the-rise-of-the-specter-part-i): Original artist page dates this work January6,2017.

Direct connection data: [current Music Atlas map](https://musicatlas.us/musicatlas.json), locally snapshotted as `atlas.json`. Parents: blackmetal, ambient, berlin_school. Children: none in this map. These are the app’s connection claims, not an assertion that music has only these influences.

### Inferences

Musical argument: The scene builds place through melodic return, restricted timbre and implied space; its later pastoral branches share that method. Contradiction: The miniature and artificial become epic through patience rather than realistic orchestration. The track jobs below are curatorial listening judgments rather than claims quoted from a source. 

### Gaps

Historical chronology is stored as `originalYear`, separately from the current catalog issue date. For reused Chicago House drafts, original-year claims are carried forward from the identified previous research/version-review files; today’s catalog lookup verifies recording metadata and US streamability, not every historical date independently. New selections combine participant/label sources and the exact catalog carriers; explicit residual chronology questions are retained below.

## 2. Which recordings won the comparison, and why?

### Takeaway

The ready sequence contains 12 recordings. No minimum length was enforced. Repeated artists remain only where their tracks demonstrate distinct development, production or song functions.

### Cited findings

- 1. Mortiis — Visjoner av en eldgammel Fremtid (Remastered) (1995): An extended repeated theme teaches how synthetic timbre becomes an inhabited place. Carrier: Ånden som Gjorde Opprør (Remastered); catalog issue 1995-11-03. Visjoner av en eldgammel Fremtid is selected as a full-length foundational work. Original Født PartI is retained in essential gaps: the full 27:37US catalog item is purchase-only; a3:11fragment was rejected. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/visjoner-av-en-eldgammel-fremtid-remastered/1299816259?i=1299816552&uo=4).
- 2. Wongraven — Over Ødemark (1995): A different keyboard and acoustic balance keeps the landscape austere. Carrier: Fjelltronen; catalog issue 1995-09-09. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/over-%C3%B8demark/1837572389?i=1837572391&uo=4).
- 3. Depressive Silence — Dreams (1996): Sustained melody shifts the imagined space toward contemplation. Carrier: Depressive Silence II; catalog issue 1996-04-30. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/dreams/1759599508?i=1759599515&uo=4).
- 4. Secret Stairways — Onward to Hy Breasail (1997): Intimate melody and soft synthetic color open another emotional register. Carrier: Enchantment of the Ring; catalog issue 1997-08-26. The seed used an album title as a song. Onward to Hy Breasail is the actual selected1997composition. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/onward-to-hy-breasail/6832630562?i=6832630677&uo=4).
- 5. Erang — Another World, Another Time (2012): A revival artist makes imagined geography an organizing compositional principle. Carrier: Tome I; catalog issue 2012-05-18. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/another-world-another-time/1527378583?i=1527378587&uo=4).
- 6. Fief — Cobblestone & Magic (2016): Miniature dance-like writing exchanges monumental darkness for an intimate scale. Carrier: I (Reissue Version) - EP; catalog issue 2016-08-01. Replaced an unverified candidate title with Cobblestone & Magic from the original2016EP, on a labeled reissue. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/cobblestone-magic/1874478674?i=1874478675&uo=4).
- 7. Thangorodrim — In Hills of Shadow Bleak and Cold (2016): Long recurring themes renew the old epic form through a newer recording. Carrier: Taur Nu Fuin (2020 Remastered Version); catalog issue 2016-07-31. Selected actual album track In Hills of Shadow Bleak and Cold rather than an unverified title;2020remaster of2016work. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/in-hills-of-shadow-bleak-and-cold/1874485861?i=1874485865&uo=4).
- 8. Old Sorcery — In a Forest Trapped (2017): Denser ambience joins the melodic framework without abandoning it. Carrier: Realms of Magickal Sorrow; catalog issue 2018-04-09. Correct title is In a Forest Trapped; original2017recording carried on2018digitalissue. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/in-a-forest-trapped/1370016764?i=1370016778&uo=4).
- 9. Quest Master — Lost Within the Caverns of Turpitude (2017): Brighter synthetic colors make the imagined setting feel exploratory. Carrier: Lost Songs of Distant Realms: Volume One; catalog issue 2017-06-10. Replaced an unverified candidate title with the actual Lost Within the Caverns of Turpitude from VolumeOne. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/lost-within-the-caverns-of-turpitude/1477419013?i=1477419025&uo=4).
- 10. Old Tower — The Rise of the Specter, Pt. I (2017): Low register and narrow melodic movement make space oppressive. Carrier: The Rise of the Spectral Horizons; catalog issue 2018-11-23. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/the-rise-of-the-specter-pt-i/1548147114?i=1548147115&uo=4).
- 11. Hole Dweller — With Dreams of Adventure, I Smoke from My Longpipe Beneath the Stars (2019): Domestic warmth makes the same world-building method sound companionable. Carrier: Flies the Coop; catalog issue 2019-08-19. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/with-dreams-of-adventure-i-smoke-from-my-longpipe/1535996901?i=1535996902&uo=4).
- 12. Fogweaver — Illuminated by Magelight (2023): A quiet closing threshold returns scale to a small repeated gesture. Carrier: Magelight; catalog issue 2023-01-13. Artist’s original Bandcamp release is January13,2023. The current Apple metadata is not used as evidence of an earlier performance date. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/illuminated-by-magelight/1662379648?i=1662379650&uo=4).

### Inferences

- Burzum — Tomhet: Important related black-metal ambient work, but a longsecond epic would crowd the contrast among independent makers.
- Grandma’s Cottage — A Cup of Tea: Pastoral branch considered; retained Hole Dweller as the stronger audible contrast.

### Gaps

- Mortiis — Født til å herske, Part I: The full 27:37 original is purchase-only in the US catalog; a3:11 fragment was rejected. The ready sequence uses the distinct full1995 Visjoner composition.

## 3. Is this ready for a later publishing batch?

### Takeaway

Every track in `tracks` has an exact official Apple US catalog ID, a returned `isStreamable: true` flag and a current November 14, 2026 check. Raw response paths are stored per track. All are explicitly import-eligible; off-platform candidates are kept outside this list. Spotify matching has **not** been checked and remains a prepublication step.

### Cited findings

The class JSON stores the ID, full URL, catalog title/artist, carrier album, duration, release date and ISRC where returned, plus the raw lookup file. US lookup responses live in `catalog-electronic/`. The current snapshot establishes availability at check time, not a guarantee of future availability. Cover art is a prepared prompt and expected file path, with existence checked separately; no new cover was generated.

### Inferences

Publish Apple Music first only after the remaining edition/chronology questions are resolved or explicitly accepted. Check the actual imported identities, chronology and public sharing, then copy that verified sequence to Spotify and check its matches. Generate the app manifest only after actual public URLs exist. Current draft URLs are catalog songs, never invented public playlist links.

### Gaps

- The foundational full1994 Mortiis performance is documented separately as a nonstreamable essential gap; no fragment is imported.
- Spotify destination matching, service order verification and public playlist URLs are pending.
- No authorization to publish is implied by this research preparation.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

DUNGEON SYNTH · A Small Keyboard Builds a World
- Shape: One small folded paper chamber unfolds into three progressively larger empty chambers, each with a single opening; scale comes from repetition rather than ornament. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#D6EAE4), flat and untinted; title ink (#29251F) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #29251F, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.title: 80.01.4.2 GOA / PSYTRANCE · The Pattern Changes Your Bearings
classes.description: 1990–present: Goa and psytrance layer twisting synth patterns over a relentless pulse, making tiny changes feel immense. FROM: Acid House, Detroit Techno, Psychedelic Rock.

classes.revelation: The beat supplies stability while interlocking timbres and patterns keep transforming the surrounding space.
classes.contradiction: A rigid kick and bass pulse can carry increasingly unstable, winding melodic and timbral movement.
classes.musicalArgument: Psychedelia emerges from sequencing, pitch and arrangement rather than a requirement for rock instrumentation.
classes.teachingNotes: Original chronology is retained separately from digital reissue dates. Historical remixes are intentional teaching objects, identified in version notes. Breakbeat Hardcore focuses its defining 1989–93 transformation and the jungle split; the other classes follow later development without claiming exhaustive coverage.

- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. classes.title: 80.01.4.4 HARDCORE TECHNO / GABBER · The Kick Becomes the Riff
classes.description: 1990s–present: Distorted kicks carry pitch as well as impact; fast repetition, abrasive stabs and shouted samples make rhythm feel like a solid wall. FROM: Detroit Techno, Breakbeat Hardcore / Rave. LED TO: Hardstyle, Hard Techno Revival.
classes.listeningQuestion: What happens when distortion turns a drum into a note?
classes.revelation: The kick is not just a timekeeper: its distortion supplies the bassline and tonal identity.
classes.contradiction: An abrasive distorted kick can become both the bass instrument and the communal hook.
classes.musicalArgument: The kick is not just a timekeeper: its distortion supplies the bassline and tonal identity.
classes.teachingNotes: Twenty tracks. Core 1990s gabber receives the main attention, then millennium hardcore and a veteran 2024 return. Dune is explicitly a happy-hardcore contrast. Name of the DJ uses the label's Extended Mixxx remaster. Angerfist's two early originals use the artist's Raise & Revolt archival disc; not remixes or DJ excerpts. DJ Rob original 1993 is cataloged as 1999. Ophidian VIP is 2004, not the 2011 compilation date. RTC God Is a Gabber first appeared in 1998 before Constrictor (1999). Holy Noise omitted because the search matched an unrelated artist.

classes.title: 80.01.4.5 DUB TECHNO · The Echo Becomes the Architecture
classes.description: 1993–present: Muted chords dissolve into echo while a steady kick holds the room together; tiny shifts in delay make repetition feel spacious. FROM: Detroit Techno, Dub.
classes.listeningQuestion: How can one chord imply an entire room?
classes.revelation: Effects are compositional voices, shaping the space and rhythm around a persistent pulse.
classes.contradiction: A nearly unchanging groove can feel spacious and alive through delay, decay and subtraction.
classes.musicalArgument: Effects are compositional voices, shaping the space and rhythm around a persistent pulse.
classes.teachingNotes: Begin with Lyot's 1992 Maurizio remix, then Basic Channel's original extended singles. Rhythm & Sound makes the Jamaican connection audible; Monolake, Fluxion and Yagya expand space into environment. Deepchord's repeated appearances trace Detroit renewal rather than implying the genre ended in Berlin. Long original tracks deliberately retained; no DJ-mix excerpts. Showcase and Vibrant Forms are artist collections of foundational singles whose individual original editions are not available in this catalog match.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

DUB TECHNO · The Echo Becomes the Architecture
- Shape: echoing impressions The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#D6EAE4), flat and untinted; title ink (#29251F) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #29251F, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.title: 80.01.4.7 HARD TECHNO REVIVAL · The Rave Returns at Full Force
classes.description: 2020s–present: Pounding kicks, trance-like rises and distorted bass compress older rave languages into sudden, high-pressure peaks. FROM: Detroit Techno, Hardcore Techno / Gabber, Trance.
classes.listeningQuestion: What makes a revival sound more intense than its sources?
classes.revelation: New production scale and abrupt contrasts make inherited hard-dance ideas feel newly physical.
classes.contradiction: The music can sound relentless while changes in kick weight, accent and silence do its expressive work.
classes.musicalArgument: New production scale and abrupt contrasts make inherited hard-dance ideas feel newly physical.
classes.teachingNotes: Three early rave/acid precursors explain the timbres. The2001–12 schranz spine prevents the false jump from1990s rave directly to today's festival sound. I HateModels and999999999 reintroduce acid/emotion, while later Alignment and Landry make the contemporary peak audible. Schranz and modern hardtechno overlap without being synonyms. ViperXXL's explicitly2012version is intentionally dated2012, not treated as its earlier original.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

MELODIC TECHNO · The Sequence Learns to Tell a Story
- Shape: descending fold The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#D6EAE4), flat and untinted; title ink (#29251F) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #29251F, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: melodic_techno

classes.title: 80.44 HARDSTYLE · The Kick Becomes the Melody
classes.description: 2000–present: Distorted kicks punch beneath grand synth themes; pitch-shifting bass tails and long breakdowns turn harsh impact into an unexpectedly melodic dance-floor language. FROM: Trance, Hardcore Techno / Gabber.
classes.listeningQuestion: How can a distorted kick drum sing?
classes.revelation: Hardstyle gives the kick both rhythmic and pitched jobs, balancing force with increasingly expansive melody.
classes.contradiction: A kick can be brutally distorted while the surrounding arrangement aims for uplift and mass singing.
classes.musicalArgument: Hardstyle gives the kick both rhythmic and pitched jobs, balancing force with increasingly expansive melody.
classes.teachingNotes: Eighteen tracks follow hard-trance tension toward pitched kick bass, euphoric melody and later rawer impact. The Second Trip deliberately uses the historically important DJ Scot Project remix, not an accidental alternate. The Prophecy is a full archival carrier exception; a modern rerecording must not replace it.

classes.title: 41.01.3.1.2.4 SLAP HOUSE · The Bass Answers the Singer
classes.description: 2019–present: Short, rubbery bass notes answer breathy vocals over a lean house kick; familiar melodies become compact, percussive hooks. FROM: Deep House, Tech House, Tropical House.
classes.listeningQuestion: How can bass timbre turn a pop song into a dance track?
classes.revelation: A clipped bass answer replaces a full instrumental chorus while keeping the singer central.
classes.contradiction: A small, tightly repeated bass gesture can carry both a club groove and a radio-sized vocal song.
classes.musicalArgument: A clipped bass answer replaces a full instrumental chorus while keeping the singer central.
classes.teachingNotes: Brazilian-bass precursor Hear Me Now precedes the2018–20 slap-house vocabulary. VIZE's percussive bass attack, Dynoro's mnemonic hook and Imanbek's shifted voice make the differences audible. Pop covers are intentional recordings, not substitute cover-artist matches. The final BellyDancer demonstrates the formula continuing into2022. Exactoriginal RosesImanbek remix selected; catalog's2018songdate is incorrect relative to official2019release. BreakingMe firstreleased2019 despite2020songmetadata.

classes.title: 41.01.3.1.7.2 BASS HOUSE / G-HOUSE · The Bassline Takes the Whole Floor
classes.description: 2014–present: House kicks support snarling bass riffs, clipped rap voices and garage swing; the drop gives low frequencies a leading role. FROM: Electro House, Brostep, UK Garage / 2-Step.
classes.listeningQuestion: Can dubstep weight move on a house pulse?
classes.revelation: A steady kick makes aggressive bass articulation dance differently from half-time dubstep.
classes.contradiction: The bass line can carry the personality normally assigned to a singer or melody.
classes.musicalArgument: A steady kick makes aggressive bass articulation dance differently from half-time dubstep.
classes.teachingNotes: Bass house is a meeting of UK garage/bassline and American electro/bass pressure, not a tidy one-producer invention. Technology/Higher precede Jauz's crystallization; NightBass recordings expose shuffle and low-end articulation. JOYRYDE and Habstrakt sharpen sounddesign while vocals return at the end. HOWSLA and ThisIsNightBassVol1 are original release vehicles, not later hitscompilations. TheBox originally circulated2015before2016streamingissue; OnFire originally2019singlebefore2020Brave.

classes.title: 72.15.1 TRIBAL GUARACHERO · The Shuffle Changes the Dance Floor
classes.description: 2000s–present: Triplet percussion, bright electronic riffs and cumbia motion create a springy shuffle; regional Mexican singing turns the club pattern into a song. FROM: Cumbia, Electro House, Technobanda. LED TO: Guaracha / Aleteo.
classes.listeningQuestion: How does a rolling shuffle change an electronic dance floor?
classes.revelation: The beat carries regional movement even as pop vocals and electronic timbres change its scale.
classes.contradiction: A looping electronic triplet groove can become both a regional dance language and a pop-song framework.
classes.musicalArgument: The beat carries regional movement even as pop vocals and electronic timbres change its scale.
classes.teachingNotes: 18 tracks rather than padding the catalog with near-identical 3BallMTY album cuts. Early underground Magdalena and DJ Mouse circulation are documented but no trustworthy Apple original was found; the sequence therefore begins with 2011 crystallization, not an invented origin. Alan Rosales and Mouse demonstrate a parallel producer lineage; El Dusty is an explicit mutation; NAAFI's original commissioned TRIBAL 2025 shows current reinvention. Zutzut, Sandunga and Lao avoid implying the style ends with mainstream crossover. Mexican tribal guarachero is distinct from later Colombian guaracha.

# 80.07.1.1 BAILE FUNK · The Bass Finds a Local Voice

Prepared, unpublished. No service playlist or app link was created.

## Listening lesson

Question: How is an imported electronic low end remade through local voices and percussion?

Revelation: Miami-bass weight becomes Portuguese chant, tamborzão patterns and shifting local vocal styles; sparse loops keep the body central.

Contradiction: A minimal backing can carry a dense account of city life.

Argument: Miami-bass weight becomes Portuguese chant, tamborzão patterns and shifting local vocal styles; sparse loops keep the body central. A minimal backing can carry a dense account of city life. The sequence first establishes the inherited gesture,then makes the defining arrangement audible,and ends with a documented mutation rather than a compulsory recent hit.

BAILE FUNK · The Bass Finds a Local Voice

The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#D6EAE4), flat and untinted; title ink (#29251F) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #29251F, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

classes.description: 1995–present: Fast breaks become tightly engineered grooves, with deep bass, spacious harmony and precise drum edits supporting everything from soulful songs to metallic pressure. FROM: Jungle. LED TO: Dubstep, UKG / Jungle-Pop Revival.
classes.listeningQuestion: What changes when the breakbeat becomes a designed rhythm section?
classes.revelation: Drum and bass holds its tempo while radically changing the density, melody and physical character of the groove.
classes.contradiction: Extreme rhythmic speed can support both weightless atmosphere and heavy physical pressure.
classes.musicalArgument: Drum and bass holds its tempo while radically changing the density, melody and physical character of the groove.
classes.teachingNotes: Eighteen tracks trace atmospheric space, technical editing, liquid songcraft, neurofunk and contemporary vocal revival. classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

DRUM AND BASS · The Bassline Organizes the Rush
- Shape: interleaving bands The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#D6EAE4), flat and untinted; title ink (#29251F) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #29251F, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.

classes.title: 41.01.3.1.5.1 JUKE · The House Beat Runs Faster
classes.description: 1990s–present: Fast kicks and clipped commands push ghetto house into nimble motion; repeated vocal fragments make the beat feel like a conversation with dancers. FROM: Ghetto House. LED TO: Footwork.
classes.listeningQuestion: What changes when house speeds up enough to challenge the feet?
classes.revelation: Speed exposes new spaces inside the bar, leading from direct commands toward more fractured patterns.
classes.contradiction: A faster beat can make the smallest gaps and vocal fragments more important than a larger arrangement.
classes.musicalArgument: Speed exposes new spaces inside the bar, leading from direct commands toward more fractured patterns.
classes.teachingNotes: Juke and footwork overlap but are not synonyms. Direct four-to-floor/chant tracks by Deeon,Slugo,Gant-Man andClent retain the party function; RP Boo,Rashad,Spinn andNate demonstrate the adjacentbattle language and latermutations. Early cassettehistory is partiallyunavailable; never substitute unrelatedsongs for3rdWurle,HailMary,orPuncho. Clent's BackUpOffMe firstcirculation1999 is grounded inartisttestimony, not2004streamingdate.

classes.title: 41.01.3.1.5.1.1 FOOTWORK · The Sample Challenges the Dancer
classes.description: 1990s–present: Rapid kicks and claps interrupt chopped voices while bass holds a slower pulse. Repeating fragments become rhythmic puzzles designed for competitive foot movement. FROM: Juke. LED TO: Chicago Bop, Deconstructed Club.
classes.listeningQuestion: How does music make room for movement at several speeds?
classes.revelation: Footwork sets fast percussion against slow bass and obsessive vocal cells, inviting the dancer to choose among competing pulses.
classes.contradiction: Music built for intensely local dance battles can reward close seated listening without losing its bodily logic.
classes.musicalArgument: Footwork sets fast percussion against slow bass and obsessive vocal cells, inviting the dancer to choose among competing pulses.
classes.teachingNotes: Contradiction: music designed for fast competitive dancing can make the pulse feel suspended. Start with repeated vocal commands; Rashad opens harmonic space, while Jlin changes the sampled language into intricate percussion. RP Boo archive dates distinguish creation from later formal release.

classes.title: 80.16.1 JERSEY CLUB · The Kick Makes the Body Stutter
classes.description: 2000s–present: Triplet kicks, chopped voices and sharp breaks turn familiar songs into dance instructions; sudden gaps invite a physical answer. FROM: Baltimore Club. LED TO: Jersey Club Rap, Deconstructed Club, Dariacore / Hyperflip.
classes.listeningQuestion: How does editing a voice create a dance step?
classes.revelation: The rhythm speaks through the arrangement of cuts as much as through the original song.
classes.contradiction: A chopped vocal can stop delivering a sentence and start directing bodies.
classes.musicalArgument: The rhythm speaks through the arrangement of cuts as much as through the original song.
classes.teachingNotes: The scene beginsaround2000; streaming selections begin2008 because DatButt and Jayhood's originalHeartbroken were not found as full licensedrecordings. UNIIQU3's repeated tracks show changing roles fromproducer to songwriter; CookieeKawaii and Bandmanrill make the song/rap transition distinct. LilUzi's export is followed by Sliink/Bandmanrill reconnecting that success to local lineage. Original-release OWSLA compilation contains RunRickyRun; not aDJmix.

classes.title: 80.15.1 NIGHTCORE · Speed Changes the Singer
classes.description: 2000s–present: Raised pitch and faster playback turn familiar voices bright and urgent; shortened phrases make emotion feel heightened and weightless. FROM: Eurodance, Trance. LED TO: Hyperpop, Sigilkore, Dariacore / Hyperflip.
classes.listeningQuestion: Does playback speed change a song or only its surface?
classes.revelation: Pitch and tempo together alter perceived character, age, urgency and emotional distance.
classes.contradiction: Changing playback speed can create a new emotional identity without changing the underlying composition.
classes.musicalArgument: Changing playback changes the felt identity of a voice. An internet editing practice becomes a community, then a compositional vocabulary and finally a mainstream release format.
classes.teachingNotes: Catalog-limited20-track class, not a complete archive of the2002scene. The Norwegian duo's formative edits and early YouTube uploads were not reliably available on Apple; no misleading modern upload is substituted as2002original. Scooter is a documented influence. DCX and Getter originals are deliberate before/after comparisons. Nightcore Reality's own site confirms its2016transition to freshly recorded originals/covers. Grimes2018original and HANA2019nightcore are intentional distinct versions. Harle,100gecs and Laura Les are explicitly influenced compositions, not remixes. Finalthree represent mainstream sped-up adoption, not the definition of all nightcore. DCX Anime Speed Mix uses the artist's2020officialsingle edition; no claim it is the first-ever accelerated Flying High. Broken Flowers original2013 reissued2015.

- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. classes.title: 80.45 DECONSTRUCTED CLUB · The Dance Floor Comes Apart
classes.description: 2010s–present: Broken kicks, metallic impacts and exposed voices interrupt familiar club patterns; gaps and collisions become the arrangement. FROM: Ballroom / Vogue, Jersey Club, Footwork.
classes.listeningQuestion: Can club music keep its physical charge when its grid breaks?
classes.revelation: Fragmentation reveals the emotional and bodily force hidden inside familiar club gestures.
classes.contradiction: A dance track can make club conventions audible by interrupting, exposing or withholding them.
classes.musicalArgument: Fragmentation reveals the emotional and bodily force hidden inside familiar club gestures.
classes.teachingNotes: A contested umbrella, not one uniform beat: Jam City and Arca fracture familiar surfaces; Janus-associated Lotic and M.E.S.H. make space and collision structural. Kamixlo, Nazar and Amnesia Scanner show different rhythmic lineages inside that procedure. Later voices reconnect abstraction to vulnerable song. Elysia Crampton's important historical contribution is discussed but her original titles were unavailable in checkedUS catalog; do not replace her with unrelated tracks. SerpentMusic likewise omitted rather than DJexcerpt.

classes.title: 51.03.1 SYNTHWAVE · The Past Becomes a Future Memory
classes.description: 2000s–present: Analog-style pulses, bright arpeggios and gated drums build an imagined cinematic past. Slow vocals and darker distortion widen the scene beyond nostalgia. FROM: Italo Disco, Synth-Pop.

classes.revelation: Timbre, spacious drums and carefully limited harmony make an invented past feel immediately familiar.
classes.contradiction: Its nostalgic surfaces are assembled with contemporary production and internet circulation.
classes.musicalArgument: Synthwave is a new compositional language of remembered soundtracks, not a historical collection of1980s records.
