classes.researchNotesText:
# 51.03.1 SYNTHWAVE · The Past Becomes a Future Memory

Prepared November 14, 2026. **Unpublished.** No service playlist has been created or changed. Course number status: proposed. Proposed numbering follows the saved current map and does not assert that every influence is a primary parent.

## 1. What should the listener learn, and how does the history support it?

### Takeaway

Question: How can an electronic production sound like a memory of a decade rather than a recording from it? Revelation: Timbre, spacious drums and carefully limited harmony make an invented past feel immediately familiar.

### Cited findings

- [Electronic Sound interviews with College, Electric Youth and Johnny Jewel](https://cdn5.f-cdn.com/files/download/232637816/ElectronicSound80_DriveFeatureIntro.pdf): Drive connected a developing electronic scene to a larger cinema audience.
- [NewRetroWave artist and label platform](https://newretrowave.com/): Current scene and artist release context; label catalog is a research feed, not proof that every nostalgic synth record belongs.

Direct connection data: [current Music Atlas map](https://musicatlas.us/musicatlas.json), locally snapshotted as `atlas.json`. Parents: italo, synthpop. Children: none in this map. These are the app’s connection claims, not an assertion that music has only these influences.

### Inferences

Musical argument: Synthwave is a new compositional language of remembered soundtracks, not a historical collection of1980s records. Contradiction: Its nostalgic surfaces are assembled with contemporary production and internet circulation. The track jobs below are curatorial listening judgments rather than claims quoted from a source. 

### Gaps

Historical chronology is stored as `originalYear`, separately from the current catalog issue date. For reused Chicago House drafts, original-year claims are carried forward from the identified previous research/version-review files; today’s catalog lookup verifies recording metadata and US streamability, not every historical date independently. New selections combine participant/label sources and the exact catalog carriers; explicit residual chronology questions are retained below.

## 2. Which recordings won the comparison, and why?

### Takeaway

The ready sequence contains 16 recordings. No minimum length was enforced. Repeated artists remain only where their tracks demonstrate distinct development, production or song functions.

### Cited findings

- 1. Kavinsky — Testarossa Autodrive (2006): A clipped electro pulse turns a fictional retro world into a dance track. Carrier: Teddy Boy; catalog issue 2010-01-01. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/testarossa-autodrive/1742757422?i=1742757425&uo=4).
- 2. College — Teenage Color (2008): Short melodic cells and warm synthetic chords build a cinematic scene. Carrier: Teenage Color - EP; catalog issue 2008-03-03. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/teenage-color/274419903?i=274419936&uo=4).
- 3. FM Attack — Dreamer (2009): A smoother harmonic language makes the retro image emotionally open. Carrier: Dreamatic; catalog issue 2009-08-29. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/dreamer/1392789660?i=1392789665&uo=4).
- 4. Lazerhawk — Overdrive (2010): Driving arpeggios give the imagined soundtrack speed and forward motion. Carrier: Redline; catalog issue 2010-01-01. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/overdrive/1275984839?i=1275984841&uo=4).
- 5. Miami Nights 1984 — Sunset Cruise (2010): A gliding melody makes mood more important than a club drop. Carrier: Early Summer; catalog issue 2010-07-05. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/sunset-cruise/1271332074?i=1271332631&uo=4).
- 6. Kavinsky — Nightcall (2010): A processed voice turns instrumental atmosphere into a compact pop song. Carrier: Nightcall; catalog issue 2010-03-26. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/nightcall/1442447952?i=1442447970&uo=4).
- 7. College — A Real Hero (feat. Electric Youth) (2010): A plain vocal and repeating bass pattern make intimacy feel cinematic. Carrier: A Real Hero - EP; catalog issue 2010-01-11. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/a-real-hero-feat-electric-youth/347480488?i=347480516&uo=4).
- 8. mitch murder — Breaking Waves (2013): Finer percussion and polished keyboard color suggest a different remembered screen world. Carrier: This is Now - Single; catalog issue 2013-12-17. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/breaking-waves/784962387?i=784962453&uo=4).
- 9. Perturbator — Humans Are Such Easy Prey (2014): Dense distortion turns the shared palette toward darksynth pressure. Carrier: Dangerous Days; catalog issue 2014-06-17. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/humans-are-such-easy-prey/865453558?i=865453705&uo=4).
- 10. Carpenter Brut — Turbo Killer (2015): Abrupt edits and aggressive timbres give the scene a harder physical attack. Carrier: Trilogy; catalog issue 2015-01-19. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/turbo-killer/1440894748?i=1440894872&uo=4).
- 11. GUNSHIP — Tech Noir (2015): Narration and a sung chorus make the imagined film explicit. Carrier: GUNSHIP; catalog issue 2015-07-24. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/tech-noir/998104509?i=998104512&uo=4).
- 12. The Midnight — Sunset (2016): A long melodic line and saxophone color bring the language into pop songcraft. Carrier: Endless Summer; catalog issue 2016-05-13. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/sunset/1758759164?i=1758759167&uo=4).
- 13. FM-84 & Ollie Wride — Running in the Night (2016): A soaring guest vocal turns the loop into an anthem. Carrier: Atlas; catalog issue 2016-04-25. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/running-in-the-night/1842390497?i=1842390499&uo=4).
- 14. Timecop1983 — On the Run (2018): A spacious instrumental keeps melody and pulse expressive without a lead singer. Carrier: Night Drive; catalog issue 2018-05-04. Original Night Drive carrier selected; the seed incorrectly described this instrumental as a duet. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/on-the-run/1373807924?i=1373807927&uo=4).
- 15. NINA — Sleepwalking (2018): A female lead and taut drums rebalance the genre around the singer. Carrier: Sleepwalking (Deluxe); catalog issue 2018-03-16. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/sleepwalking/1355873114?i=1355873134&uo=4).
- 16. The Midnight — Deep Blue (2020): Newer pop production keeps the remembered palette while widening its scale. Carrier: Monsters; catalog issue 2020-07-10. Original studio composition or explicitly named original remix. Archival/reissue carriers are distinguished from originalYear. [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/deep-blue/1508063533?i=1508063546&uo=4).

### Inferences

- John Carpenter — Assault on Precinct13: Influential original film language, reserved as a comparison; this class begins with the new scene itself.
- M83 — Midnight City: Related indietronica crossover; omitted to leave the defining synthwave producers more room.

### Gaps

No essential off-platform candidate is required to complete the verified sequence. Wider scene coverage remains possible; this is a bounded listening argument rather than a comprehensive discography.

## 3. Is this ready for a later publishing batch?

### Takeaway

Every track in `tracks` has an exact official Apple US catalog ID, a returned `isStreamable: true` flag and a current November 14, 2026 check. Raw response paths are stored per track. All are explicitly import-eligible; off-platform candidates are kept outside this list. Spotify matching has **not** been checked and remains a prepublication step.

### Cited findings

The class JSON stores the ID, full URL, catalog title/artist, carrier album, duration, release date and ISRC where returned, plus the raw lookup file. US lookup responses live in `catalog-electronic/`. The current snapshot establishes availability at check time, not a guarantee of future availability. Cover art is a prepared prompt and expected file path, with existence checked separately; no new cover was generated.

### Inferences

Publish Apple Music first only after the remaining edition/chronology questions are resolved or explicitly accepted. Check the actual imported identities, chronology and public sharing, then copy that verified sequence to Spotify and check its matches. Generate the app manifest only after actual public URLs exist. Current draft URLs are catalog songs, never invented public playlist links.

### Gaps

- No additional class-specific catalog issue is recorded.
- Spotify destination matching, service order verification and public playlist URLs are pending.
- No authorization to publish is implied by this research preparation.

classes.coverPrompt:
Draw this

SYNTHWAVE · The Past Becomes a Future Memory
- Shape: One plain doorway opens onto a second smaller doorway printed on a folded sheet, their slightly misaligned outlines making a remembered room rather than a real landscape. The artwork stays in the lower 55% of the canvas, with clear space between it and the subtitle; nothing in the upper right.
- Colors: shelf ground (#9E2A2B), flat and untinted; title ink (#EDE4D1) repeated within the artwork, with restrained mustard and muted coral accents; rich ink ground, texture must not wash out the color.
- Type: #EDE4D1, never tinted to match the artwork. Preserve the exact title and subtitle above, including accents.
- Style: fictional late-1960s/early-1970s educational music textbook; layered flat screen-print forms and deepening ink overlaps, strong negative space; one idea.
- Typography: fixed series footprint at upper left, the title starting at the top margin; title in an ultra-condensed, heavy grotesque sans serif, all caps, clean and crisp; subtitle directly below in a bold grotesque sans, title case; the title runs the full width from the left margin to the right margin, scaled up until it fills that width; stack multi-word titles one word per line only when a single line would squeeze the letters narrower than the typeface's normal condensed proportions; never shrink the title to accommodate artwork. No numbers, labels, or any text other than the title and subtitle.
- Detail: flat, simplified forms like a screen print; each object reduced to two or three solid color shapes, close to a silhouette; no shading, highlights, gradients, or surface texture on any object; a small number of distinct elements, favoring a few large shapes over many small ones; no fine interior detail such as leaf veins, window panes, railings, or wood grain (the aged finish is separate); repeated elements stay countable, never a swarm.
- Full bleed: no frame, border, or mat; the ground color runs to every edge of the canvas; the worn raw-paper edge is only a thin frayed rim, never a border.
- Finish: aged record sleeve; subtle printed-paper grain over the whole cover; ink very slightly faded but colors still rich; a few faint scratches and one or two thin crease lines running diagonally across the cover; softly rounded corners with worn, frayed edges showing a little raw paper. The aging must not change the typeface; lettering stays crisp and even, only lightly touched by the grain. On framed artist covers, the aging applies to the inset panel only; the gallery white border stays clean.
No performers, instruments, records, flags, logos or genre stereotypes.

Suggested filename without extension: synthwave
